mlb.all_star_game_event_model.label: All-Star Game result and MVP model: league talent, exhibition usage and MVP credit given the winning team
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.mechanism: The exhibition has equal-stakes, short-stint pitcher usage and substitution rules, so the result is close to a coin flip and the MVP comes from the winning team's players with the most plate appearances and highlights.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.rationale: KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBASGMVP resolve on a one-off game: league strength differences are tiny relative to variance, and MVP depends on the winning side, plate appearances and extra-base or home-run events.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.measurement: P(league wins) from the difference in selected-roster strength (summed projected wOBA/ERA by lineup and pitching slots) mapped through the game-win logistic with a compressed slope (about 0.5 of the regular-season slope, to be estimated from 2010-2025 results). P(MVP = player) = P(his league wins) x share, share = softmax of expected plate appearances x per-PA highlight probability (HR, multi-hit) with a pitcher-specific term for the winning pitcher. As-of: roster announcement and starting lineups.
raw_data: All-Star Game box scores 2000-2025
roster ratings

mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.label: Draft lottery odds by prior-season record and eligibility rules
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.mechanism: Draft position is set by a lottery among non-playoff clubs whose odds are fixed by prior-season record, with restrictions on consecutive top-pick wins.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.rationale: KXMLBDRAFTPICK is not an award or race: the probability of a given pick is a lottery function of record rank, the number of lottery slots and the consecutive-win restrictions.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.measurement: Odds table P(pick = j | record rank r) from the official lottery rules (non-playoff clubs, odds by reverse record rank, lottery covering the first picks, restrictions on repeated winners and revenue-sharing recipients), with record ranks from the final standings and tiebreaker; simulate the lottery. Units: probability by pick slot. As-of: final standings. The numeric odds table for the draft in question is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED here.
free_sources: MLB draft lottery rules and odds table
raw_data: final standings
published lottery odds table and restrictions

mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of award outcomes for combination markets
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.mechanism: A combination market pays only if several awards go to specified outcomes, whose probabilities are correlated through shared player performance and team narrative.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.rationale: KXMLBAWARDCOMBO needs P(A and B), not the product: an MVP and Cy Young from the same team are positively dependent via team success, while two MVPs in different leagues are nearly independent; the electorates also differ.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.measurement: Estimate pairwise dependence between award outcomes by a Gaussian copula fitted to 25 seasons of winners (same-team indicator, shared-electorate indicator) shrunk to independence with k = 10 seasons; P(A and B) = C(P(A), P(B); rho). Units: probability. As-of: after finalists are announced.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by season and league

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.label: League order-statistic engine for best/worst record, 100+ losses, longest losing streak and team strikeouts (simulation method; its inputs are mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_vintage)
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.mechanism: The extreme among thirty teams is determined by each team's talent distribution and the shared schedule.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.rationale: Existing inputs address single games; extremes require a league-wide simulation where each team's outcome is drawn jointly, ties are tracked for $1/N payouts, and streak and strikeout statistics are computed from game-level sequences.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.measurement: Simulate remaining games for 30 teams using team talent posterior (mean, sd) and schedule; record final wins, the longest loss streak per team (run-length of simulated sequence) and team strikeouts (batters faced x team K rate with pitching staff K% projection, sd from game-level variance). Outputs: P(team is unique best), P(tied for best with N teams), expected payout with $1/N rounding; P(wins <= 62 for 100 losses). 20k simulations; calibrate sd to historical. As-of: daily. Units: probabilities.
free_sources: MLB Stats API results and schedule
raw_data: team game logs; remaining schedule; team projections; team K% and batters faced

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR, SB and remaining games: HR_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_HR * PA_rest, SB_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_SB * PA_rest x opportunity; PA_rest from games remaining x P(play) x PA per game; correlation via shared PA factor and a latent role; compute P(HR >= 50 and SB >= 40) by simulation. Rates from rest-of-season projection blended with current-season pace (shrunk k = 250 PA). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: player daily stats; ROS projections; sprint speed; injury status

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.label: Extreme pitch-speed distribution (probability of a 107+ mph pitch given pitcher max velocities and pitch counts)
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.mechanism: The fastest pitch of a season is the maximum over pitches of a speed distribution with a heavy upper tail for a few pitchers.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.rationale: A threshold of 107.0 mph is at the edge of the known distribution; the probability depends on a handful of pitchers' maximum fastball velocities, their usage and number of high-velocity pitches, and the tracking system measuring release speed.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.measurement: For each pitcher: fit a generalized extreme value (GEV) or exponential tail to the pitcher's fastball speeds (top 1% of pitches) using the last 2 seasons; expected number of fastballs in the remaining window N_i; P(max_i >= 107) = 1 - exp(-N_i * P(speed >= 107 | fastball)). Combine across pitchers P(any) = 1 - Prod(1 - p_i). Include postseason pitches only for playoff teams. Units: probability. As-of: daily, with current-season maximum. CAVEATS: 107 mph lies beyond the observed record (about 105-106 mph tracked, unverified here), so an exponential tail fitted to the top 1% extrapolates; a physical-ceiling cap or generalised-Pareto fit with a finite endpoint is required. Independence across pitchers in P(any) = 1 - prod(1 - p_i) is an assumption (shared parks, radar calibration).
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed for fastballs by pitcher; usage counts

mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.label: Series exact score distribution (4-0, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3 for each team) from game win probabilities with dependence
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.mechanism: Exact series scores follow from the sequence of game outcomes and the best-of format.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.rationale: Each score has a different probability and depends on home-field pattern, starters and dependence between games; independent games underpricing sweeps and seven-game series.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.measurement: Simulate series with game probabilities p_i from starter-specific model; shared strength offset N(0, 0.04); stop at four wins; compute probabilities of the eight exact scores. Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 or 2-3-2 as applicable. Calibrate offset sd on best-of-seven history since 2012. As-of: after each game. Units: probabilities.
raw_data: series-level: games, scores, starters, home pattern; game probabilities

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.label: Longest winning streak: extreme-value distribution given team win probabilities and remaining games
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.mechanism: The longest win streak across teams is the maximum over runs of consecutive wins; the season-level maximum is an extreme value.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.rationale: Season streak markets are filed in this archetype but are not inning markets; the winning team is the one with the longest run, with ties paying $1/N, so the exact distribution of the maximum run for each team (given per-game win probability, mostly 0.4-0.65) determines the odds.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.measurement: For team i with games remaining n_i, current streak c_i and per-game win prob p_ij: P(longest streak >= L) computed by a run-length Markov chain; account for heterogeneity of p_ij by opponent and home/away, and current maximum across league to date. P(team has strict maximum) = Prod over rivals (1 - ...) with Monte Carlo and tie share 1/N (payout rounded down). Streak serial correlation assumed zero unless tested. As-of: daily. Units: probability. Postponed, suspended and cancelled games are excluded from the sequence; the streak model assumes independent games conditional on p_ij, so serial correlation and doubleheader order are assumptions.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule and results
raw_data: team game log: date, win/loss, opponent, home flag; remaining schedule; current streaks and league maxima

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.label: Lockout and shortened-season scenario: P(lockout), start/end dates and games lost under each scenario
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.mechanism: A CBA lockout after Dec 1 2026 could delay opening day and cancel games, so season-games and opening-day outcomes are mixtures over scenarios.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.rationale: A 600-game strike equals roughly a quarter of the 2,430-game schedule and a May 31 opening cutoff is a long delay; both are plausible stoppage thresholds. In 2021-22 the lockout postponed opening day by about one week with no games lost (to my knowledge), but 1994-95 lost the end of one season and the start of the next; the distribution of games lost is heavy-tailed with a large mass at zero.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.measurement: Scenario mixture: P(no lockout) from negotiation state (own timestamped coding of reports, ordinal 0-4); conditional on a lockout, the stoppage end date drawn from a survival model with prior from 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22 (3 events, strongly shrunk) updated by negotiation stage; games lost = schedule games before the agreed start date after a compressed ramp-up (about 3 weeks of spring training), with doubleheaders making up part. Output: P(first regular-season game before May 31 2027) and P(games played > 600) = P(games lost < 1,830). As-of: daily.
raw_data: CBA expiry date
labour news timeline
2027 schedule and games per date
1990, 1994-95, 2021-22 stoppage records

mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.label: All-30-team talent posteriors with projection vintage, remaining schedule and head-to-head structure
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.mechanism: League-wide order statistics need every team's win-probability distribution, correlated through the shared schedule.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.rationale: Best record, worst record, 100+ losses and the longest-streak markets are maxima over 30 teams; the engine inputs are the 30 posterior means and sds, the remaining schedule and projection vintages, not the engine itself.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.measurement: For each team i: posterior mean p_i and sd s_i from preseason projection (average of ZiPS/Steamer, prior sd 0.04) updated by pythagenpat win% with conjugate normal weights (k = s_game^2/s0^2 about 156 games), as-of daily; remaining schedule with opponent posteriors and home flags; projection vintage stored at each date so backtests use only information available then. Output: 30 x (p_i, s_i), the 30-team opponent matrix and remaining games. As-of: after each day's games.
free_sources: FanGraphs ZiPS/Steamer (current only; vintages need own capture)
MLB Stats API standings and schedule
raw_data: daily standings and run differential
30-team schedule
archived projection vintages (own capture)

mlb.spring_training_playing_time_regime.label: Spring-training playing-time regime: share of innings and plate appearances by MLB regulars versus non-roster and minor-league players, split-squad flag and tie rule
mlb.spring_training_playing_time_regime.mechanism: Spring-game outcomes depend on who plays the late innings, which is set by ramp-up schedules, split squads and the number of non-roster players each club carries, not by regular-season talent.
mlb.spring_training_playing_time_regime.rationale: KXMLBSTGAME settles on a spring game, where regulars play perhaps a third of the innings and the rest goes to depth players of uneven quality; a club playing a split-squad game sends a weaker roster, and spring games may end tied, so regular-season ratings mislead without this adjustment.
mlb.spring_training_playing_time_regime.measurement: For each club and game: expected innings share of 40-man players = sum over announced pitchers of planned innings / 9 and over the posted lineup of expected PA share (regulars about 2 PA, then substitutes); quality of the remainder from projected minor-league equivalents (wOBA and FIP) shrunk toward replacement with k = 100 PA; split-squad flag from the schedule; tie rate by league (Cactus, Grapefruit) from 2015-2026 spring results. Team strength for the game = innings-share-weighted average of regular and depth ratings. As-of: posted spring lineup and probable pitchers; units: run-value per game.
free_sources: MLB.com spring-training lineups and box scores (free_scrape)
raw_data: spring-training box scores with innings by pitcher and PA by batter
split-squad schedule flags
non-roster invitee lists by club
spring tie results

mlb.special_event_game_staging.label: Special-event game staging probability (Field of Dreams and similar one-off venue games) for a season
mlb.special_event_game_staging.mechanism: A one-off venue game exists only if the league schedules it, which depends on venue readiness, broadcaster commitment and the schedule calendar.
mlb.special_event_game_staging.rationale: Every club market resolves No if no 2027 game is staged, so this single probability scales all club probabilities; it is driven by site redevelopment status in Dyersville, the national broadcaster's special-event slate, the league's other special events that compete for the same mid-season window, and labour risk around the Dec 1 2026 CBA expiry.
mlb.special_event_game_staging.measurement: P(staged in season Y) = logistic(b0 + b1*venue_ready_flag + b2*broadcaster_slot_confirmed + b3*prior_season_staged + b4*announced_by_date_flag) times (1 - P(labour stoppage cancels or delays the event past the market close)); fit b on special-event venue games 2016-2026 (Fort Bragg, Williamsport Little League Classic, Field of Dreams, Rickwood, international series) with a weakly informative prior (sd 1 on each coefficient) because N is under 30; labour factor from mlb.labor_stoppage_regime. As-of: latest dated venue, broadcaster or league report; units: probability.
free_sources: MLB press releases and schedule announcements (free_scrape)
Local Iowa press on the Dyersville site (free_scrape)
raw_data: special-event games by season with announcement date, venue, participants and whether played
dated venue-status and broadcaster reports

mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.label: Special-event participant selection affinity by club pair (distance, marketability, recency, home-date cost, schedule fit)
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.mechanism: The league and broadcaster pick the pair that maximises regional attendance and national audience subject to the schedule matrix and a home club willing to move a home date.
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.rationale: Club probabilities are a pair choice, not independent events: Midwestern clubs dominate, national draws are paired with regional clubs, recent participants are less likely, and the designated home club loses gate revenue at a small temporary stadium; the pairing must already exist as a mid-season series in the 2027 matrix.
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.measurement: Conditional logit over unordered club pairs: utility = a1*log(min road distance of the two clubs to Dyersville, miles) + a2*(TV market size rank sum) + a3*(either club used in the last 3 stagings) + a4*(pair is a division or traditional rival) + a5*(pair has a mid-season series in the released or projected matrix); fit on special-event venue selections 2016-2026 with coefficients shrunk to a distance-only model (shrinkage weight k = 10 events). Club marginal = sum of pair probabilities containing the club (sums to 2). As-of: matrix and report date; units: probability.
free_sources: Club market-size and stadium distance data (public geography)
raw_data: club home-city coordinates and distance to Dyersville, Iowa
special-event participant pairs by year
season schedule matrix by series
TV market size by club

mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.label: Draft prospect selection signal: consensus board rank, signability and reported team links for a given pick slot
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.mechanism: Which player a club takes at a slot follows the consensus ranking adjusted for club preference, bonus-pool strategy (underslot deals) and signability, with late reports of pre-draft agreements.
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.rationale: A draft-pick market resolves on an identity or slot, so the input must turn public rankings and reported links into a selection probability; the bonus-pool system makes underslot picks common at the top, so rank alone mis-prices.
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.measurement: For each prospect and slot j: average rank across public boards (MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, FanGraphs) at the as-of date; signability flag (college senior, high-school commitment strength); reported links per club from timestamped mock drafts and reports (count of independent outlets). Fit a conditional-logit choice model per slot on 2012-2025 drafts with club-level shrinkage (k = 5 drafts); P(player at slot) chained over earlier slots by sequential sampling. Units: probability. As-of: timestamp of the latest board and report; lottery outcome as a conditioning input for slot ownership.
free_sources: MLB Pipeline and FanGraphs draft boards (free_scrape)
raw_data: prospect board ranks by date
draft results by slot 2012-2025
timestamped mock drafts and reported links

mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.label: World Baseball Classic national-team strength from confirmed rosters (projected WAR by role, pitch-limit-adjusted pitching depth)
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.mechanism: National-team win probability depends on rostered player talent, with pitching value reweighted for tournament pitch limits that shorten starts and shift innings to relievers.
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.rationale: KXMLBWORLD resolves on a short tournament between federations whose strength changes with each MLB player's decision to participate and with club or insurance limits on pitchers; club-based ratings do not apply, and pitch limits make relief depth worth more than in MLB.
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.measurement: For each federation, sum projected full-season WAR (the tournament is in March, before the season) per 600 PA (hitters) and per 150 IP (pitchers) from the most recent projection system for rostered players; pitchers weighted by expected tournament innings under the round pitch limits (about 65/80/95 pitches by round, to be verified) and relievers by available appearances; non-MLB players mapped via league-equivalence factors (NPB, KBO, CPBL, minors) shrunk to replacement with k = 200 PA. Convert rating differences to single-game win probability with a log5 model fitted on 2006-2026 tournament games; simulate pools and bracket. As-of: final roster announcement date; units: probability.
free_sources: World Baseball Classic official rosters and results (free_scrape)
raw_data: confirmed national-team rosters with announcement dates
player projections and league-equivalence factors
tournament game results 2006-2026
pool and bracket format with tiebreaker rules

mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.label: League-wide playoff home-run count: games remaining by bracket path times per-game home-run expectation with game-level dispersion
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.mechanism: Total playoff home runs equal home runs so far plus a sum over the remaining playoff games, each contributing a negative-binomial count driven by the two lineups, the park and weather; the number of remaining games is itself random.
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.rationale: KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS is a threshold on a sum over a random number of games, so most of its variance late in October comes from how many games remain (sweeps versus seven-game series) rather than from per-game HR rates; per-game rates differ by park and cold weather, and games share weather and pitcher-day factors.
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.measurement: H0 = official playoff HR so far. For each remaining game g on each bracket path (probabilities from mlb.bracket_path_enumeration): lambda_g = sum over both teams of projected HR per PA (rest-of-season hitter projections vs the probable starter and bullpen, shrunk to team rate with k = 300 PA) x expected PA (about 38 per team) x park-and-weather factor (mlb.park_specific_xhr deciles). Game count ~ NB(lambda_g, phi) with phi from mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion. P(H0 + sum >= N) by Monte Carlo over paths and series lengths (20k draws). Calibrate total-HR-per-postseason predictions on 2015-2025 postseasons. Units: count and probability. As-of: after each playoff game.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason box scores
raw_data: postseason HR by game
probable starters and lineups per game
park and weather by game

mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.label: Scoreless-streak survival: per-out probability a pitcher records an out with no run charged, and P(reach N innings) from the current streak
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.mechanism: A scoreless streak extends by one third of an inning per out recorded without a run charged to the pitcher and ends at the first charged run, so reaching N is a survival product over the outs still needed.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.rationale: KXMLBSISTREAK settles on consecutive scoreless innings counted in thirds; elite starters post per-inning scoreless rates near 0.80, so a ten-inning gap has probability around 0.1 and is extremely sensitive to the per-inning rate, opponents, parks and whether runners he leaves on base later score. The contract does not say whether unearned runs break the streak, so both definitions must be computed.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.measurement: Per-inning scoreless probability q_j for start j = P(0 runs in a half-inning) from a base-out Markov chain using the pitcher's projected K%, BB%, HR/PA and BABIP (shrunk to league with k = 300 batters faced) against the opponent lineup and park of start j, plus P(an inherited runner he leaves scores) from the bullpen's strand rate. Expected outs per start from sp_workload. P(reach N) = P(product over the 3*(N-current) needed outs of per-out survival, accumulated across remaining starts before season end, with no charged run); computed both with all runs and earned runs only. Units: probability; as-of: after each start.
free_sources: Baseball Savant and MLB Stats API play-by-play (free)
raw_data: play-by-play with base-out state and run charged to pitcher
pitcher game logs with outs recorded
remaining schedule and probable starters

mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.label: All-Star Game roster, starters and planned participation (who plays, in which slot, for how many innings)
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.mechanism: Each hitter's plate appearances and each pitcher's batters faced in the exhibition are set by roster composition, the two managers' substitution habits and the announced pitching order, not by a season-long role.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.rationale: A player who is named but enters in the 6th inning gets one or two PAs; a starter gets two or three. Pitchers are normally used for one inning each, so strikeouts come from many arms facing a few batters. Withdrawn players are replaced by commissioner picks, which changes both pool and slots. Every per-player ASG market is first a participation question.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.measurement: Per ASG year 2012-2025 build a table of plate appearances by lineup slot (starter vs reserve entry inning) and batters faced by pitcher role (starter, middle, closer-type). Estimate P(plays at all | selected, position, reserve status) and E[PA | plays] by league/manager, shrunk to the 14-year pooled mean with k = 3 games. For the target year use the posted rosters, listed starters and probable pitchers as of the market timestamp; refresh at lineup announcement (about 1-2 hours before first pitch). Output per player: P(any PA), PA distribution over {0,1,2,3,4}; per pitcher: P(pitches), expected BF.
free_sources: MLB Stats API all-star game feed (free)
raw_data: asg box score: player, team, entry inning, PA, AB, H, HR, K, BF, IP by year
roster announcements with timestamps, withdrawals and replacements

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.label: All-Star Game format and tiebreak regime for the year (innings, extra-inning or swing-off rule, pitcher limits)
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.mechanism: The rulebook for the year decides how long the exhibition lasts if tied and whether the tiebreak produces countable events.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.rationale: Since 2022 (first actually used in 2025) a game tied after nine innings goes to a swing-off (three hitters per side) instead of extra innings, and earlier years used automatic-runner extras; the 2026 rules text confirms a swing-off can end the game. Player hit and HR props exclude swing-off statistics, but the combined game-HR total does not say so, so the regime changes both the winner distribution and which events can count.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Record per year: scheduled innings, extra-inning rule (automatic runner or not), tiebreak mechanism if any, pitch-count or innings limits, DH use in both leagues, roster size. Encode as categorical regime flags; reweight historical games by regime similarity (weight 1 for same regime, 0.4 otherwise). Collect the commissioner's announcement of rule changes before the event and flag any change announced after market open. P(tie after 9) taken from 14 years of scores as a prior around 0.05-0.10, to be checked.
free_sources: MLB press releases and official ASG rules notes (free_scrape)
MLB Stats API game rules fields (free)
raw_data: per-year ASG rule notes and final scorelines by inning

mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.label: Home Run Derby field: who is invited, who accepts, withdrawal and replacement hazard, seeding
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.mechanism: The Derby field is a self-selected set of hitters, so qualifier and winner markets depend on acceptance, injury withdrawals and replacement choices.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.rationale: Top sluggers often decline, and replacements arrive days before the event (Murakami was the eighth and final addition in 2026 after returning from the injured list). The field is both an input and a target: KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL settles Yes on selection even if the player then withdraws, while every other Derby market resolves No for a non-participant. Round 1 in 2026 is pool play, so seeding no longer sets Round 1 opponents; semifinal pairings follow Round 1 rank.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.measurement: For each year 2015-2025 record the invited list at announcement dates, acceptance, final eight, replacements and seeding rule. Model P(accept | rank in season HR, prior participation, age, team home park hosting, injury status) as a logistic with shrinkage k = 5 per feature group. As-of: use announcements dated before the market snapshot; late replacement flagged separately. Output: P(player in final eight) and the seed table.
raw_data: derby participants with announcement dates, replacements, seeding by year
season HR to date at announcement

mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.label: Home Run Derby round output under the 2026 swing-capped format: swings allotted, per-swing HR rate, last-swing extension and advancement
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.mechanism: With a fixed swing allotment (20 in Round 1, 15 in the semifinal and final) a round's homers equal the sum of per-swing HR indicators plus a geometric extension when the last allotted swing is a homer; the clock, pitcher pace and bonus time no longer exist.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.rationale: Under swing caps volume is fixed, so the levers are per-swing HR rate, selectivity (takes appear not to count against the allotment, so waiting for a hittable pitch costs nothing but time) and the quality of the hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher. Round 1 is an eight-man pool where the top four advance, so the advancement threshold depends on the whole field's rates, not on one opponent.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.measurement: Per hitter: p = P(HR | swing) estimated from season barrel rate, pulled fly-ball rate and max-EV percentile (through the day before the Derby) mapped to Derby HR per swing using 2015-2025 Derby swing logs (timed-format years, swing outcomes only, not volume), shrunk to the pooled Derby mean with k = 40 swings, adjusted by the BP-pitcher term and host-park carry. Round HR ~ Binomial(n_r, p) + extension E where E is geometric with P(last swing HR) x p/(1-p) expected extra homers; n_r = 20, 15, 15. Fatigue as a multiplicative decay on p per round (prior 0.97, shrunk). Simulate the pool, the longest-HR Round 1 tiebreak and three-swing swing-offs. As-of: field and rulebook at the snapshot.
free_sources: Baseball Savant Statcast season batted balls (free)
MLB.com Derby results and swing logs (free_scrape)
Press reports of the 2026 format (AP, June 2026) (free)
raw_data: derby swing-level log: participant, round, swing number, take or swing, result, distance, exit velocity, BP pitcher
per-year Derby rulebook: swings per round, extension rule, tiebreaks

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.label: Derby extremes: probability of 500+ foot homers, longest homer and peak exit velocity over the event
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.mechanism: Longest-HR, 500+ ft count and highest exit velocity are maxima of batted-ball distributions over a few hundred swings, so they live in the upper tail of each hitter's power distribution.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.rationale: A batter's average HR distance says little about whether he reaches 500 or 525 ft. Tail behaviour needs top-decile EV and distance, park and wind carry, and the number of homers he gets, which under the 2026 format is set by rounds reached. Longest and highest-EV series are dead-heated at the league's reported precision, so rounding matters.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.measurement: For each hitter fit a generalized Pareto tail to HR distances and exit velocities above his own 85th percentile over 3 seasons of Statcast (min 25 exceedances, else borrow league shape and use own scale shrunk with k = 15), plus a Derby uplift estimated from 2015-2025 Derby versus in-game tails. Number of draws per hitter = homers from the throughput model, i.e. 20 Round 1 swings, plus 15 more if he reaches the semifinal and 15 more in the final, plus extensions; this makes extremes depend on bracket advancement, not clock. Adjust for host-park carry from mlb.park_specific_xhr and weather. Simulate jointly with the throughput model because the Round 1 tie rule (longest HR) couples totals and distances; report P(any >= 525 ft), P(500+ count >= k), P(each hitter has longest), P(each hitter has highest EV HR). As-of: games through the previous day.
free_sources: Baseball Savant Statcast batted-ball distance and EV (free)
raw_data: statcast batted balls: batter, hit_distance_sc, launch_speed, launch_angle, park, game_date
derby historical longest HR and max EV by year

mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.label: Home Run Derby batting-practice pitcher chosen by each hitter: identity, pitch speed and location consistency, past Derby results
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.mechanism: Per-swing HR rate depends on how hittable and repeatable the batting-practice pitches are; each hitter picks his own pitcher (often a coach or relative), so the pitcher is a hitter-specific matchup input.
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.rationale: With swings fixed, a pitcher who puts the ball in the hitter's preferred zone at a steady speed raises HR per swing directly, and an erratic one forces takes and weak swings. Pitcher history across hitters (the same coach pitching several Derbies) gives a partial pooling base.
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.measurement: Record pitcher identity per participant from announcements. Where Statcast Derby pitch tracking exists: mean and SD of release speed and plate location distance from the hitter's preferred zone per pitch, 2015-2025. Pitcher effect = random effect on logit P(HR | swing) in a hitter + pitcher model fitted on Derby swing logs, shrunk to 0 with k = 60 swings; unknown pitchers get the pooled mean. As-of: pitcher announcement before the snapshot.
free_sources: MLB.com and club announcements of Derby pitchers (free_scrape)
Baseball Savant Derby tracking where published (free_limited)
raw_data: participant, BP pitcher name, year
derby pitch-level speed and location if tracked

mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star Game MVP selection: panel plus fan ballot credit model over game performance, team result and star profile
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The MVP is chosen after the game by a selection panel with a fan ballot component, so it rewards a decisive hit or homer for the winning league, weighted by name recognition.
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: The award almost always goes to a player on the winning side with the game's most visible contribution (go-ahead homer, multi-hit game); fan voting adds a star-name bias for close calls. A swing-off decision changes credit because swing-off events are visible but may not count as game statistics.
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: From ASG box scores 2000-2025 build per-player credit features: winning-side flag, HR, RBI, go-ahead or tying event flag, hits, strikeouts for pitchers, inning of key event, and a star index (career All-Star selections, social follower rank). Fit a conditional logit for P(MVP | game events) and integrate over simulated game outcomes from the participation and per-PA models. Panel and fan weights taken from the year's MLB announcement (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED until checked). As-of: rosters and lineups at the snapshot.
free_sources: Baseball-Reference All-Star Game box scores and MVP list (free)
MLB press releases on MVP voting (free_scrape)
raw_data: ASG MVP winners by year with game line
ASG play-by-play with win probability added per event

mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.label: Futures Game roster strength: prospect hitting and pitching quality by league from minor-league stats translated to a common scale
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.mechanism: The Futures Game is a seven-inning NL vs AL exhibition of prospects with short pitcher stints, so the winner depends on translated minor-league talent of the two rosters and on how many innings each arm covers.
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.rationale: Talent is minor-league and heterogeneous (Double-A teenagers next to Triple-A arms), so major-league ratings do not exist; translated stats and prospect grades are the only strength measure. The game is short, so variance is high and the talent edge is small.
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.measurement: For each rostered prospect compute translated wRC+ and FIP from the current minor-league season using level factors (MLE: Triple-A 0.90, Double-A 0.82 of MLB-equivalent rate, to be calibrated), blended with prospect-list grades (weight 0.3), shrunk to the level mean with k = 150 PA or 40 IP. Team strength = PA-weighted lineup score and innings-weighted pitching score under a seven-inning usage plan from 2023-2025 box scores. As-of: roster announcement and replacements before the snapshot.
raw_data: Futures Game rosters and box scores by year
minor-league batting and pitching lines by level for rostered prospects

mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.label: MLB-MLBPA bargaining positions: proposals on the economic system, salary-cap or floor demands, and public statements
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.mechanism: Whether a deal is reached before expiry is set by the gap between owner and union proposals on the economic system and by each side's stated red lines.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.rationale: The sticking points in baseball talks are structural (revenue sharing, payroll limits, luxury-tax design, pre-arbitration pay) rather than incremental. A salary-cap demand by owners against a union that has historically refused any cap produces a hard gap that does not close by small concessions, so stated red lines matter more than the number of meetings.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.measurement: Code each public proposal or leak by topic (cap/floor, tax thresholds, revenue share, service-time, arbitration, draft, schedule length) as {proposed by, date, source tier}. Compute a gap index = number of topics with incompatible stated positions / topics open, updated at each bargaining session; add a red-line flag when either side calls an item a non-starter. As-of: public reports timestamped before the snapshot; discount single-source leaks to weight 0.5 until confirmed by a second outlet.
raw_data: dated list of proposals by topic and party
statements by commissioner and union leadership with timestamps

mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.label: Bargaining calendar hazard: days to expiry, owners' lockout decision date, spring-training and scheduled-opener deadlines
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.mechanism: A deal can only arrive at certain points on a fixed calendar, and the hazard of agreement rises near binding deadlines.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.rationale: The CBA expiry on December 1, 2026 is the first deadline; the second is the February pitchers-and-catchers report date; the third is the scheduled opener. The market threshold date of May 31 and the 600-game strike value sit after all three, so the relevant question is the cumulative hazard through several deadlines, not at one.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.measurement: Build a discrete-time hazard on weekly steps from expiry to the scheduled opener plus 60 days: h(t) = P(agreement in week t | none yet), with features: weeks to the next hard deadline (spline), lockout in force flag, number of formal sessions in last 14 days, gap index. Fit on 1972, 1973, 1976, 1980-81, 1985, 1990, 1994-95, 2002, 2016 and 2021-22 episodes with strong shrinkage; map to P(first regular-season game before May 31) = P(agreement by the date implied by scheduled opening plus allowed ramp-up (about 3-4 weeks for spring training)). Dates taken from the published schedule and CBA text as of the snapshot.
free_sources: CBA text and prior CBA expiry timeline (free)
raw_data: calendar of deadlines: CBA expiry, report dates, scheduled opening day, break points
historical stoppage episodes with start, end and cancelled games

mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.label: Reference class of MLB and comparable league stoppages: duration, cancelled games and ramp-up needed before play
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.mechanism: With very few comparable events the best prior for stoppage length is the historical distribution across baseball and other major leagues, adjusted for how much money is at stake.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.rationale: Only about nine baseball stoppages exist, ranging from a few days to a cancelled postseason, and 2021-22 delayed but did not shorten the schedule. Cross-sport lockouts (NHL 2004-05 lost the season, NBA 2011 lost about 16 games) add a heavy tail the baseball sample alone does not show.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.measurement: Table of MLB stoppages: type (strike or lockout), start, end, duration in days, regular-season games cancelled, spring training lost, ramp-up days between agreement and first game. Cross-sport table for NHL/NBA/NFL. Fit a mixture: P(short) from MLB (deal before first scheduled game), P(long) from pooled leagues; weight MLB episodes 1.0 and others 0.3; add a Beta prior (a=2, b=2) on P(any regular-season games cancelled). As-of: static history, update for any new episode.
free_sources: Wikipedia and league histories for NHL/NBA lockouts (free)
raw_data: episode table: dates, games lost, ramp-up days

mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.label: Leverage state: owners' revenue and broadcast contract position versus players' strike-fund and salary exposure
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.mechanism: A stoppage lasts as long as both sides' costs of waiting stay below their expected gain, which depends on revenue, television contracts, player earnings at risk and reserves.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.rationale: Regional sports network disruptions, national TV renewals and a rising luxury tax change who loses more from lost games. A lockout is a bet that players, who miss paychecks, concede first. Those costs are observable only through proxies, so the input must be built from revenue indicators and public finance data.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.measurement: Construct a leverage ratio = owners' cost of lost games per week (national media revenue share + gate + local media at risk, from public estimates and league-wide revenue reports) divided by players' cost per week (average salary share of the schedule, with a distribution weighting by arbitration and minimum-salary players) and a strike-fund and reserve indicator for the union. Update quarterly; treat as ordinal (-1, 0, +1) when exact data is missing. As-of: latest annual report or credible estimate before the snapshot.
free_sources: Forbes/Sportico franchise valuations and revenue estimates (free_limited)
MLBPA and league financial disclosures where public (free_limited)
raw_data: league revenue estimates and media contract terms
player payroll by tier, union reserves where disclosed

mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.label: Schedule map from start date to games played: games per calendar day, scheduled finish date and make-up capacity
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.mechanism: Games played in a shortened season equals scheduled games on dates after the first game, plus any games the league can add through doubleheaders and make-up days.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.rationale: Of the 2,430 scheduled games, the share that remain after a given delay depends on how the schedule is spread (about 13 to 15 games per calendar day on average, with fewer on Mondays and in April) and on whether MLB prefers to compress by doubleheaders, cancel series or play 162 by extending the season. The 600-game strike corresponds to a very late start or season cancellation.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.measurement: From the published 2027 schedule compute N(d) = scheduled games on or after date d for each d, and D(d) = days until the last scheduled regular-season day. Estimate recoverable games R(d) = min(doubleheader capacity, off days that can be used) with doubleheader capacity = 0.25 x open dates (calibrated on 2021-22, where the full 162 was played after the delay, a compression through a few extra doubleheaders). Predicted games played G(d) = N(d) + R(d), cutoff d* such that G(d*) = 600. As-of: schedule file version at snapshot.
raw_data: schedule by date with games per day
doubleheader and off-day inventory

mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.label: Go/no-go decision on staging a truncated season: minimum viable season length, postseason media revenue and pro-rated pay terms
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.mechanism: Fewer than 601 league games happens only if no season is staged or one starts in roughly mid-August or later; that is a joint owner-union decision to play a short season for postseason and TV revenue (2020) or to cancel (1994-95), not schedule arithmetic.
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.rationale: At 13-15 league games per day, 600 games is about 40-46 days of play, so make-up capacity never matters at this strike. The deciding question is whether, late in the calendar, the parties agree a minimum season: postseason national media money is large relative to a short regular season, which pushed the 2020 deal to a 60-game season (898 games played), while in 1994-95 the parties cancelled the postseason. Pay pro-rating and service-time credit decide whether players accept a short season.
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.measurement: Model P(season staged | no deal by date d) as a logistic in days remaining before the scheduled postseason start (minimum viable season assumed 40-60 team games, i.e. 600-900 league games, plus a 3-week ramp-up), an indicator that postseason media payments are contingent on games being played (from public contract reporting), and an indicator that a pro-rated pay and service-time framework is already agreed. Anchor with 2020 (staged, 60 games, agreement on terms imposed late June) and 1994-95 (postseason cancelled); prior P(staged | late deal) = 0.6 with Beta(3,2), updated on reports. Output P(games > 600) = P(deal or imposed season leaves >= 601 games).
free_sources: Press archives of the 2020 return-to-play negotiations (free)
raw_data: dated chronology of season-length proposals and decisions (2020, 1994-95)
postseason media contract terms as publicly reported

mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.label: Impasse, implemented terms, replacement-player and labour-board/injunction state of the dispute
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.mechanism: A stoppage can end without agreement: owners may declare bargaining impasse and implement terms or field replacement players, and the union may file unfair-labour-practice charges leading to an NLRB complaint and a federal injunction that restores prior terms and returns players.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.rationale: The 1994-95 strike ended when the NLRB obtained a federal injunction (March 31, 1995) restoring the expired terms, after owners had used replacement players in spring training. This route changes both timing and what counts: replacement-player games could be official regular-season games, and an injunction can start a season without a new CBA.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.measurement: Track as an ordinal state with dates: 0 bargaining, 1 lockout or strike, 2 impasse declared or terms implemented, 3 replacement players signed or scheduled, 4 ULP charge filed, 5 NLRB complaint or 10(j) petition, 6 injunction granted or denied. Hazard of season start = baseline from the bargaining hazard plus a state-specific term (state 6 granted implies return within about 3 weeks, from 1995). Sources timestamped; NLRB docket entries verified by case number. As-of: filings and announcements before the snapshot.
free_sources: Federal court dockets via PACER (paid) and press coverage (free)
raw_data: dated legal and impasse events with case numbers
replacement-player announcements

mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.label: Playoff home-game allocation table: designated home team per game by round, seed and series length, with the as-played home log
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.mechanism: Games hosted is a deterministic function of seed, rounds reached and series length through the format's home pattern; this input is that allocation rule plus the record of which club was the designated home team in each game already played.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.rationale: The path convolution itself is a model output; the information needed is the allocation rule. It is easy to get wrong: a best-of-3 Wild Card Series is hosted entirely by seeds 3-4, so they can reach 13 hosted games, while bye seeds reach at most 11 and seeds 5-6 host nothing in round one. Designated home team, not venue, must be logged because relocation is possible.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.measurement: Static table h(round, seed role, length): Wild Card Series best-of-3, higher seed (3 or 4) hosts every game (2 or 3), lower seed 0; Division Series 2-2-1, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G5 (2-3), lower seed G3, G4 (1-2); LCS 2-3-2 by seed and World Series 2-3-2 by regular-season record, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G6, G7 (2-4), lower seed G3-G5 (2-3). Combine with seed probabilities (mlb.season_sim, mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path) and series-length probabilities from the series model in the model layer, not here. As-of: format of the target season; per-game designated home team and venue logged after each game.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game feed: home team and venue per game (free)
raw_data: postseason format table: round, length, home pattern by seed
per-game designated home team, venue, date

mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.label: Projected starter for each game of the series after off days, with short-rest and bullpen-game probabilities
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.mechanism: Which starter pitches game k depends on the announced rotation, off days, ace usage on short rest and the chance of a bullpen game.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.rationale: In a short series the top starters pitch more games, so team strength is not constant across games. Game 5 of a division series or Game 7 may feature an ace on short rest or an opener. Postseason off days compress the rotation to three or four men, making the per-game win probability a sequence rather than a single number.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.measurement: For each remaining game build a probability table P(starter = s) from rotation order, days of rest (off days count), number of starts so far, manager history of three- versus four-man rotations (postseason 2015-2025), injuries, and statements by managers (weight 0.5 until announced). Convert to per-game win probability by log5 with starter quality (SIERA/Stuff+ blended with 3-year projection, shrinkage k = 60 IP) plus bullpen-day penalty for P(opener). As-of: announcements through the snapshot time; probables update with each game. Postponements: a rainout shifts every later game by a day and adds rest, so recompute rest days and starter eligibility after any postponement in the official schedule.
raw_data: probable starters by game with timestamps
pitcher days of rest, innings and pitch counts in series

mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.label: Cumulative bullpen workload across the series: relievers' pitches on consecutive days and off-day resets
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.mechanism: High-leverage relievers cannot pitch every day, so fatigue and unavailability accumulate over games and reset on off days.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.rationale: In a short series managers use the best relievers heavily, which makes the closer's availability in game 5 depend on usage in games 3 and 4 and on the schedule of off days. This is a dynamic availability state, unlike the regular-season rest rules, and it can reduce a stronger team's edge late in the series.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.measurement: Track reliever pitches in the last 1, 2 and 3 days from play-by-play; flag unavailability when pitches >= 25 yesterday or 3 consecutive days (thresholds from regular-season 2021-25 usage, calibrated per manager, shrunk k = 30 appearances). Compute team leverage-weighted bullpen availability score = sum over relievers of (talent x P(available)), as of the lineup-card time. Reset on off days using the observed usage patterns in postseason series. Postseason extra innings use no automatic runner, so log extra-inning length per game; a 12+ inning game removes several relievers for one to two days and is the main source of multi-game depletion.
raw_data: reliever pitch counts by date, leverage index of entries, off-day calendar

mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.label: Postseason roster eligibility between rounds: injured-player replacement, roster resets and who can be on the series roster
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.mechanism: Each series has its own submitted roster, so an injured player may return or be replaced between rounds, which changes team strength round by round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.rationale: A team's strength entering the league championship series is not the same roster as in the division series; hitters and pitchers can be swapped between rounds under league rules. This matters for hosting-count markets that span several rounds and for any series where injuries occur in the previous round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.measurement: For each team log submitted postseason rosters by round (2012-2025), flag injured-list players with return timelines and replacements; compute expected strength change = sum of WAR-above-replacement difference of players added minus removed, using projections (ZiPS/Steamer rest-of-season rates). As-of: roster submission deadline and public injury reports; unconfirmed flagged as probability weights.
free_sources: MLB transactions page and postseason roster announcements (free_scrape)
raw_data: roster submissions per round, injury returns, replacements

mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.label: Market-free per-game win probability for each remaining game of a series, built from starters, bullpen availability, lineup and home edge
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.mechanism: The series is a first-to-N path through game probabilities that differ by game because the starter, bullpen state and home team change; this input is the vector p_1..p_N those components produce.
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.rationale: This replaces the series length and exact-score distributions as the true information input: those are deterministic transforms of this vector plus within-series dependence. Building it from components (not from series or game prices, which are benchmarks only) is what allows it to move when a rotation is announced or a closer is unavailable.
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.measurement: For game k: logit p_k = a0 + b1 x (postseason-weighted team rating difference, runs per game) + b2 x (probable-starter RA9 projection difference x expected starter innings share, about 0.55 in recent postseasons) + b3 x (availability-weighted bullpen rating difference x relief share) + b4 x lineup-vs-hand wRC+ difference + home term (park-specific, shrunk to about +0.035 win probability, k = 300 games). Starter identity is a mixture over mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game. Fit b on 2012-2025 postseason and late regular-season games with ridge shrinkage. No market price, line or implied probability enters. As-of: probables and availability at the snapshot.
free_sources: MLB Stats API probables and box scores (free)
FanGraphs and Baseball Savant player rates (free)
raw_data: per-game probable starters, reliever availability flags, lineups, home team
player rate projections as of the snapshot

mlb.series_game_dependence.label: Within-series dependence of game outcomes beyond the modelled starter and fatigue effects (residual correlation parameter)
mlb.series_game_dependence.mechanism: If game results share an unmodelled common factor (injury carried through the series, a mis-rated team), the series score distribution is wider than the independent-games path implies: more sweeps and more seventh games.
mlb.series_game_dependence.rationale: Spread (sweep) and exact-score cells are tail cells of the score distribution, so a small positive correlation shifts them far more than it shifts the winner probability. The parameter must be estimated, not assumed zero, and its uncertainty carried.
mlb.series_game_dependence.measurement: Fit a game-level logistic model on 1995-2025 postseason games using pregame component predictions as offset; add a series-level random effect and estimate its standard deviation by marginal likelihood; convert to an equivalent pairwise correlation rho with a bootstrap interval over series. Compare predicted versus observed frequency of 4-0 and 4-3 results by best-of-N format. As-of: static history, refit each offseason.
raw_data: postseason game results with series id, game number, starters, home team

mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.label: Final first-round draft order: which club holds each overall slot 1-10 after lottery, reverse-record fill, CBT pick moves and inserted compensation picks
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.mechanism: An exact-slot contract is a statement about the club holding that slot, so the slot-to-club map must be resolved before any prospect preference applies.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.rationale: The lottery fixes picks 1-6 only; slots 7-18 follow reverse record among non-playoff clubs that missed the lottery, a club far over the top luxury-tax threshold has its first pick moved back ten places (outside the top six), and a prior-year unsigned first-rounder yields an inserted compensation pick one slot later, which renumbers every later pick. First-round picks cannot be traded in MLB, so unlike other leagues the map is fixed once these rules run.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.measurement: Start from the lottery result (or simulated lottery draws before it), apply lottery-ineligibility placement (reviewer-cited 2022 CBA rule, not verified here: clubs barred from the lottery, i.e. revenue-sharing payors that won in consecutive years and recipients that won in three straight years, pick no higher than 10th, which can reshuffle slots 7-10), then fill the remaining slots through 18 by reverse prior-season winning percentage with the official tiebreak, apply the CBT ten-slot penalty to clubs whose CBT payroll exceeded the base threshold by $40M or more (the third surcharge tier, not the highest $60M tier; highest pick moved back ten places unless it is a top-6 pick), insert prior-year failed-to-sign compensation picks at original slot + 1, then renumber; output club_id per overall slot with a timestamp of the official order release. Before the lottery output P(club holds slot k) from 10,000 lottery simulations.
raw_data: final standings with tiebreaks for the prior season
lottery result by slot
CBT payroll status by club
prior-year unsigned first-round picks

mlb.prospect_consensus_board.label: Consensus pre-draft prospect ranking: mean and dispersion of the named player's rank across independent public draft boards
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.mechanism: Clubs' private boards are correlated with public expert boards, so the public consensus rank and its spread locate where a prospect is likely to come off the board.
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.rationale: A prospect ranked 3rd by every board has a narrow selection window; one ranked between 4th and 20th has a wide one, and exact-slot probability is driven as much by that disagreement as by the mean. Boards are expert scouting judgements, not prices, and they update through spring (college season, high-school showcases), so vintage matters.
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.measurement: Collect the final pre-draft top-250 lists from MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, ESPN, FanGraphs and The Athletic; for each prospect compute mean rank, median, standard deviation and min-max range across boards, plus the rank change over the last 30 days. Weight boards equally unless historical rank-to-pick error by source (2015-2025 drafts) says otherwise; store each board with its publication timestamp.
raw_data: board name, publication date, prospect name, rank, position, school, age

mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.label: Final mock drafts and insider reports linking named prospects to specific clubs, including reported pre-draft bonus agreements
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.mechanism: In the last 48 hours before the draft, insiders report which club is on which player and which prospects agreed below-slot bonuses, and these links often fix top picks.
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.rationale: Top MLB picks are frequently pre-negotiated: the club and advisor agree a bonus before the pick, and national writers publish these links. A report that club X is 'in on' player Y at slot 5 can move the exact-slot probability far more than any scouting change. Mock drafts are writer forecasts, not market prices, but must be timestamped and scored for source accuracy.
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.measurement: Scrape every published mock and draft-day report from the final 14 days with timestamp, writer, slot, club and prospect; per writer compute historical exact-slot hit rate and top-10 hit rate over 2015-2025 first rounds with a Beta prior (k = 20 picks). Produce per prospect: share of final mocks placing him at each slot and a reliability-weighted slot distribution, frozen at the market snapshot timestamp.
raw_data: mock draft: writer, version timestamp, slot, club, prospect
draft-day report text with timestamp and claimed club link
reported club workouts/visits and advisor-linked bonus talk

mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.label: Prospect scouting and performance profile: tool grades, opponent-adjusted college or showcase stats, tracked batted-ball and pitch data, age and demographic class
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.mechanism: Clubs rank prospects by projected major-league value, which they build from tools, performance against level of competition, tracking data and age relative to class.
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.rationale: Analytic clubs weight college performance and age heavily (younger-for-class college hitters with strong contact and exit velocity rise), while scouting-led clubs weight tools and projection. Knowing why a prospect is ranked tells which clubs are likely to deviate from consensus on him, which matters at an exact slot.
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.measurement: For college players: wOBA, K% and BB% adjusted for conference strength, exit-velocity 90th percentile and chase rate from TrackMan or Synergy where published, and wood-bat summer league line (Cape Cod); for pitchers: velocity, spin, K-BB%. For high-school players: showcase metrics (exit velocity, 60-yard time, max fastball). Record age on draft day and class (HS, 4-year college, junior college); z-score each metric within class.
raw_data: college season batting and pitching lines by game with opponent
summer league stats
showcase measurables with event date
date of birth

mlb.prospect_medical_signability.label: Prospect medical red flags and signability (college commitment leverage, advisor bonus demand, age-eligibility status)
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.mechanism: A prospect with a reported medical issue or a high bonus demand backed by a strong college commitment can slide well below his talent rank.
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.rationale: Pre-draft physicals (via the MLB Draft Combine medical program) and leaked bonus demands are classic causes of draft-day slides. High-school players can refuse to sign and go to college, so clubs avoid demanding players at slots whose value is below their ask; four-year college seniors have no leverage and go under slot.
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.measurement: Binary and graded flags from reports in the final 30 days: medical concern reported (yes/no, body part, source), surgery history, reported bonus ask relative to the assigned slot value of each slot 1-15, college commitment strength (program tier), and eligibility class. Also record agency/advisor identity with its historical share of clients signing over slot or returning to school, club pre-draft workouts and private visits as publicly reported, and any report that the prospect shared medicals selectively. Convert to an expected slide in slots by fitting historical slides of flagged players against their board rank (2012-2025).
free_sources: MLB Pipeline and Baseball America draft reports (free_limited)
raw_data: report text and timestamp with medical or bonus-demand claims
combine attendance and medical participation
college commitment by prospect
advisor/agency by prospect
reported club workouts and private visits

mlb.club_draft_tendency.label: Club drafting tendency at top picks: college vs high school, hitter vs pitcher, position, underslot frequency and deviation from consensus, by front-office regime
mlb.club_draft_tendency.mechanism: Each club picks from its own board; persistent front-office preferences make some clubs predictable deviators from consensus.
mlb.club_draft_tendency.rationale: Some clubs have taken college bats with nearly every high first-round pick, others take prep pitchers or reach for underslot deals to spread pool money. Tendencies hold only within a scouting director and general manager regime, so a regime change resets the prior.
mlb.club_draft_tendency.measurement: For each club, first-round and supplemental picks 2012-2025 restricted to the current scouting-director/GM tenure: share college, share pitcher, mean (pick slot minus consensus board rank), share signed below slot value. Shrink to league means with k = 6 picks; flag regime changes with the hire date.
raw_data: historical picks: year, slot, club, player, school type, position, signing bonus
front-office personnel tenure dates

mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.label: Bonus-pool and slot-value structure: assigned slot values per pick, club pool size, overage tax and forfeiture thresholds, and incentives for underslot top picks
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.mechanism: Clubs maximise total draft value under a hard-ish bonus pool, so taking a cheaper player at a high slot frees money for later picks.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.rationale: Exceeding the pool by up to 5% costs a 75% tax and larger overages cost future first-round picks, so pools act as a budget constraint. Clubs with several early picks or a deep later class have strong incentives to sign the slot-5 pick below value, which favours college seniors and players with low leverage over the consensus talent.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.measurement: Official slot values for picks 1-75 and each club's total pool for the draft year; per club compute (pool total, number of picks in the top 75, share of pool in its first pick). Historical below-slot discount at slots 1-10: (bonus minus slot)/slot by club and class, 2012-2025. Output a per-club underslot propensity score in [0,1].
raw_data: slot value by pick and year
club pool totals
signing bonus by pick

mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.label: Sequential draft selection engine: club-specific rank-ordered choice over the remaining pool, giving P(prospect taken at slot k) and P(taken by slot N)
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.mechanism: The draft is a sequence of without-replacement choices: each club's choice depends on who remains, so pick probabilities across prospects and slots are jointly constrained.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.rationale: Exact-slot probabilities for one prospect over slots 1..N plus P(not in top N) must sum to one, and across prospects each slot is taken by exactly one player. A rank-ordered (Plackett-Luce) choice model with club-specific utility shifts captures cascades: if two players go earlier than expected, the named player is more likely to fall to a given slot. It is a derived model that consumes the information inputs, so it is listed only as the structural constraint on them.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.measurement: Utility of prospect i for club c = -alpha * consensus rank_i + club tendency terms (college, pitcher, underslot fit) + insider-report shift + medical/signability penalty + Gumbel noise; simulate slots 1..20 sequentially 50,000 times, removing chosen players. Fit alpha and the noise scale on 2012-2025 first rounds by maximum likelihood; output P(slot = k) for k = 1..20 and cumulative P(slot <= 10) per prospect.
free_sources: derived from the inputs above and historical draft results (derived)
raw_data: historical first-round picks with pre-draft board ranks
per-club tendency and pool features
current board, report and flag tables

mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.label: Candidate pool of pitchers able to approach the velocity threshold: tracked peak velocity, top-pitch distribution and minor-league peaks of possible call-ups
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.mechanism: Only pitchers whose tracked peak already sits within roughly two mph of the threshold have any realistic chance of a single pitch exceeding it.
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.rationale: Pitch speed is bounded by the arm: league-wide, fewer than a dozen pitchers have tracked pitches above 104 mph in a season, and the all-time tracked maxima sit near 105-106 mph. For the 'any pitcher' series the pool, not the average pitcher, carries the probability; prospects with Statcast-tracked AAA peaks can join it mid-season.
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.measurement: From Statcast pitch-level release_speed (MLB) and Hawk-Eye AAA data: for each pitcher in the last three seasons compute season max, 99.9th and 99th percentile of fastball speed, number of pitches at or above 103 and 104 mph, and age; include in the pool if 3-season max >= 103.0 mph or AAA max >= 103.0. Apply an aging adjustment of about -0.2 to -0.3 mph per year after age 27 to percentiles, shrunk by pitch counts. As-of: daily.
raw_data: pitch-level: pitcher, date, game_pk, pitch_type, release_speed, level

mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.label: Remaining exposure to max-effort fastballs: expected count of high-velocity fastballs per candidate over the rest of the season and postseason
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.mechanism: The chance that the season maximum crosses a threshold rises with the number of near-peak attempts, so exposure is the volume term of the extreme.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.rationale: A closer throws perhaps 600-900 fastballs a year, nearly all at full effort; a starter throws more but paces, so only first-inning and high-leverage fastballs approach his ceiling. Exposure must count near-peak attempts, not all pitches, and must add postseason games only with the team's probability of playing them.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.measurement: Per candidate: projected remaining appearances (role, health) x fastballs per appearance x share of fastballs within 1.5 mph of his season max (from his own pitch-level data, last 60 days with shrinkage to prior season, k = 300 pitches); add postseason expected appearances = P(team reaches each round) x expected games x appearance rate. Units: expected near-peak fastballs. As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule and standings (free)
raw_data: pitch-level fastball speeds with appearance id
appearance logs and roles
remaining schedule and playoff probabilities

mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.label: Within-pitcher situational velocity lift: change in fastball speed with leverage, postseason, inning of appearance, pitch number, count, days of rest and temperature
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.mechanism: A pitcher's top speed on a given pitch is his baseline plus situational lifts; record pitches cluster in high-adrenaline, rested, warm, early-in-outing situations.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.rationale: Velocity rises in the postseason and in high-leverage spots, falls after consecutive days of work and with pitch count, and is expected to be lower in colder air (effect size unverified, see velo_temperature_effect). Because the threshold sits in the extreme tail, a lift of half a mph multiplies the exceedance probability many times.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.measurement: Mixed model on fastball release_speed: pitcher random intercept and slope by season; fixed effects for leverage index bucket, postseason flag, pitch number within appearance (spline), two-strike count, days since last appearance (0,1,2,3+), game temperature (F) and roof closed; fit on 2021-2025 Statcast pitches; output per-situation additive lift in mph with standard errors, applied to each candidate's tail model.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game weather fields (free)
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed with game_pk, inning, pitch number, count, leverage proxy
game temperature and roof status
appearance dates

mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.label: Pitch-speed tracking calibration: Hawk-Eye release-speed definition, park-level speed offsets, data revisions and displayed precision
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.mechanism: A record pitch is a measurement; park-to-park calibration offsets and later corrections can move a reading by a few tenths of a mph, which is decisive at the edge.
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.rationale: Statcast reports release speed, which differs from the old PITCHf/x 50-ft reading, so historical records are not directly comparable. Park-specific biases have been documented for radar systems, scoreboard and broadcast readings differ from Statcast, and MLB sometimes revises pitch data after the game. Settlement on '107.0+' versus '107+' interacts with one-decimal rounding.
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.measurement: For each park and season estimate the speed offset as the mean residual of visiting pitchers' fastball speeds at that park versus their speeds elsewhere (pitcher fixed effects, minimum 2,000 pitches per park-season, shrink to zero with k = 5,000). Track revisions by re-pulling pitch data 1, 7 and 30 days after each game and recording changes in release_speed. Record displayed precision (one decimal).
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed by park and game
repeated pulls of the same games at different dates

mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.label: Forward injury hazard for elite-velocity pitchers: probability of losing the remaining season to elbow or shoulder injury, conditional on velocity and workload history
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.mechanism: The pitchers who could set a velocity record are the ones most exposed to UCL and shoulder injuries, so the pool erodes during the season.
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.rationale: Current IL status is not enough: the question is how much of the remaining exposure each candidate will actually pitch. Velocity is a known risk factor for elbow injury, and a velocity drop is often the first sign. The named pitcher's market is near zero if he is shut down; the any-pitcher market loses its tail contributors one by one.
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time hazard per 30-day window of a 60+ day IL placement for elbow or shoulder, fitted on 2015-2025 pitchers with covariates: peak fastball velocity, age, prior UCL surgery, innings in prior 12 months, recent velocity z-score drop (from rolling starts); output expected share of remaining exposure lost. Point-in-time: use only IL transactions and velocity known at the as-of date.
free_sources: Jon Roegele Tommy John surgery list (free)
raw_data: IL transactions with dates and body part
pitcher velocity histories
surgery history list

mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.label: Pitcher role and effort regime: starter pacing versus one-inning max-effort relief, and probability of a role change (including postseason bullpen use of starters)
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.mechanism: Starters pace velocity over 90-100 pitches while one-inning relievers throw every pitch near peak, so the same arm reaches higher speeds in relief.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.rationale: A hard-throwing starter typically sits 1.5-3 mph above his starting average when used in short relief. Postseason clubs often move starters to the bullpen, and clubs sometimes convert prospects to relief. The named-pitcher probability depends on which role he will occupy for how many appearances.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.measurement: Per candidate: current role (SP/RP/opener) and P(role change) over the remaining window from club statements and history; role-specific fastball speed distributions estimated from pitchers who switched role in 2015-2025 (within-pitcher difference in 99th-percentile speed, SP to RP, shrunk to the league mean shift). Output role-weighted tail parameters and exposure.
raw_data: appearance logs with role (start/relief) and innings
pitch-level speeds by appearance

mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.label: Frequency and persistence of anomalous release-speed readings in the raw live tracking feed versus the later corrected Statcast record
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.mechanism: With 107 mph above every tracked pitch, a YES can come from a feed glitch, mis-tagged pitch or unit error that is published (and possibly later corrected) rather than from a physical pitch.
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.rationale: The physical tail near 107 is almost empty, so the probability of a spurious reading can dominate the physical path. What counts depends on whether Kalshi settles on the first published reading or the corrected one, which the rules do not say. Calibration of Savant re-pulls alone cannot see readings that were removed before the first public pull.
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.measurement: Poll the MLB Stats API live game feed for every game during play and store each pitch's startSpeed with capture timestamp and pitch id; after 1, 7 and 30 days re-pull Savant release_speed for the same pitch. Per season compute: (a) count of live-feed pitches with speed >= 104.0 or more than 3.0 mph above that pitcher's season 99th percentile, (b) share of those that changed by more than 1.0 mph or vanished in later pulls, (c) median hours to correction. Output an expected number of anomalous readings >= threshold per season, with a Beta(0.5,0.5) prior on the per-game rate. As-of: daily, own-captured snapshots only.
free_sources: MLB Stats API live game feed polling (own_capture)
raw_data: live-feed pitch snapshots: game_pk, pitch id, startSpeed, capture timestamp
Savant release_speed for the same pitches at +1, +7 and +30 days
game-level notes of tracking outages or corrections

game_side.target: Which team wins the game (and by how many runs for spread/margin contracts), settled after the final out including extra innings unless the wording says otherwise.
game_side.mechanism: Win probability follows from the expected run difference: starter run prevention for the innings he works, bullpen quality for the rest, lineup quality against the specific starter's handedness and arsenal, and park/weather/umpire scaling of both offences. Home field adds a small edge. Because late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starter, weather) moves the line, the model's value comes from timely incorporation and from regressing luck-heavy team results; margin and spread contracts additionally need the run-difference distribution including extra-innings tie breaking.

inputs.why: Starter true talent drives early-inning run prevention for both teams.
Expected innings decide how much the bullpen pitches.
Confirmed lineup replaces probable lineups; absent stars change offence.
Lineup quality against this starter's handedness is the offence driver.
Bullpen availability decides run prevention after the starter exits.
Quality of relievers beyond fatigue snapshot.
