contract_review.settlement_definition: Thirty-one live series of voted awards, selections and statistical races after the reconciliation, all with sampled rules. Award winners (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie, Reliever, Manager and Executive of the Year, Hank Aaron, Comeback, ALCS/NLCS/World Series MVP) pay on the official winner; the series-MVP texts pay $1/N to each official co-winner, and AL Comeback Player lists a separate 'Tie/Co-Winners' outcome, while the other award texts have no co-winner clause. KXMLBAWARDFIN pays if the player is named a finalist 'as reported by one of the Source Agencies', resolving all No if finalists are not announced before the winner. Monthly and weekly awards (Player and Pitcher of the Month, Player of the Week) pay $1/N rounded down when several candidates share the award. KXMLBALLSTAR pays Yes if the player is selected to his league's All-Star team, even if he does not participate. KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts playoff statistics only, resolves No for a non-playing participant, pays tied leaders proportionally and considers statistical corrections only if made before expiration. KXMLBSEASONHR (50+ HR) and KXMLBSTATCOUNT (50 HR and 40 SB) count regular-season games only; KXMLBTRIPLECROWN requires leading the league in batting average, home runs and RBIs over the regular season; KXMLBTEAMSTAT (sampled: most strikeouts thrown by a team's staff) pays $1/N on ties. Silver Slugger (sampled: NL team award) and Gold Glove (sampled: NL pitcher) name specific awards. No text names a source of truth other than the finalist 'Source Agencies'. All-Star Game, Derby and draft series are in other archetypes.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official awards announcements and ballots (BBWAA/MLB), official league statistics for leader markets; the finalist market names 'Source Agencies' without listing them in the sample.
variants_and_edge_cases: Finalist versus winner: the finalist market has a fixed field (three finalists per league per award) selected from ballot ranks, so probability is rank-based (top three) rather than winner-based; the announcement condition adds a No branch.

Voter populations differ and are not all BBWAA: BBWAA ballots decide MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year and Manager of the Year; the Rivera and Hoffman Reliever of the Year awards are, to my knowledge, voted by a panel of retired relievers; Hank Aaron, Comeback Player and Executive awards have other electorates (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED, see lea_electorates); managers and coaches vote Gold Glove (with a defensive-metric component) and the positional Silver Sluggers, while the electorate of the team Silver Slugger sampled in KXMLBSS is unverified; fans, players and the league choose All-Stars Each needs its own model.
Statistical races (Triple Crown) are joint order statistics of three correlated categories with rate-stat qualification rules and tie handling; counting windows (regular season only) matter.

Eligibility rules (rookie status limits on at-bats, innings and days on the active roster) can make candidate sets differ from the obvious field; most award texts are silent on co-winners, which only the series-MVP texts, the monthly and weekly awards and the AL Comeback 'Tie/Co-Winners' outcome address.

Postseason awards and leaders: series MVPs are named from the winning team in nearly all cases and pay $1/N on co-winners; the playoff runs leader depends on how many games a player's team plays, so it is a joint bracket-and-production event; a non-playing participant resolves No rather than voiding.
Manager and Executive of the Year (moved here): Manager of the Year is a BBWAA award voted before the postseason; the executive award's electorate is unverified (see lea_eoty_electorate).

Silver Slugger and Gold Glove series name specific awards: the sampled KXMLBSS market is the NL Silver Slugger for Team (a team-offence award) and KXMLBGG is the NL Gold Glove for Pitcher, so each series needs the award's own electorate and candidate pool (team offence for SS Team; pitcher fielding, where the SABR Defensive Index is thin, for GG); a tie for a Triple Crown category lead is not addressed.

Selection versus participation: KXMLBALLSTAR resolves Yes on selection even without participation, so injury replacements named later count as separate selections; monthly and weekly awards split the payout among co-recipients.

Team counting race (KXMLBTEAMSTAT, sampled: most strikeouts thrown) is a thirty-team order statistic of staff strikeouts over the regular season with $1/N on ties; other stat variants of the series are unseen.

player_participation.label: Player participation (plays / starts / appears)
player_participation.target: Whether a named player plays or starts in a game, per the contract's definition.
player_participation.mechanism: Participation is determined by manager decisions (rest days, platoon sits), injury status and late scratches, resolved mostly when the lineup card posts; before then it is a probability from rest-day patterns, handedness of the opposing starter and injury news, afterwards it is near-certain except for in-game substitution cases. The edge is timing relative to market close and the exact definition (starts vs appears).

inputs.why: Lineup card timing and confirmation.
Starter/platoon/bench role: a player's role determines whether he starts and how many PAs he gets, which drives participation and counting-stat markets.
Rest after night games and travel.
IL status and late scratches: absences change lineup/rotation composition and late scratches can void or reprice player markets.
Manager platoon and substitution style.
Schedule density and doubleheaders.
Opposing starter handedness drives platoon sits.
Beat-writer reports on availability.
Definition of plays/starts and void rules.
Lineup posting vs market close.
Clinched or eliminated teams rest regulars and call up prospects; the policy is manager-specific and timestamped by announcement.
The contract's No-on-replacement rule makes this hazard a term in the price after the card posts.
KXMLBPITCH and similar windows depend on rehab timing rather than games played.
Converts single-game probabilities to window-level probability with correct correlation structure.
Gives the starting-pitcher participation market a rotation-based mechanism instead of the hitter lineup chain.
Defines the missing call-up inputs for the debut series.

interactions.hypothesis: Rest pattern x opposing handedness: platoon players sit against same-handed starters, so P(start) combines rest-day pattern and the starter's handedness.
Lineup posting time x market close: probabilities are mixtures until the card posts, so the posting timestamp relative to close defines the information advantage.
Injury vintage x scratch risk: players listed day-to-day have elevated scratch probability late, so injury reports and warm-up news interact with lineup confirmation.

A platoon player sits against same-handed starters and rests after night games, so start probability is a conditional product of role, opposing hand and rest pattern; for everyday players only the rest pattern matters, so the effect of handedness is gated by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit start logistic with role x hand x rest-day terms and compare calibration by role.

interactions.hypothesis: Before the card posts the probability is a mixture of manager patterns, after posting it collapses to the scratch hazard; the transition is a step in time at posting, so the value of information is concentrated at posting relative to market close.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model error before and after the observed posting timestamp for historical games.

interactions.hypothesis: Window availability is a survival process: rehab stage determines time to activation, injury hazard after activation determines early failure, and the number of games available determines how many opportunities there are; failures across games are correlated through the absorbing state.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate window-level probability with and without correlated absorption; compare to naive product of per-game probabilities.

interactions.hypothesis: After a team clinches a seed or is eliminated, rest probability switches regime: regulars sit and prospects play, with the size of the switch depending on the manager's style and on whether seeding still matters; before clinching the baseline pattern applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate start probability by standings state (clinched/eliminated) and manager; test the discontinuity at clinching date.

interactions.hypothesis: Role changes (call-up, trade, injury replacement) announced by news shift start probability at a discrete date, so the window model must restart its per-game probabilities at the change; the number of games after the change drives the window probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Segment games by role-change date and compare window predictions with piecewise versus constant role probabilities.

interactions.hypothesis: For a returning starting pitcher the window market is Yes only if activation comes early enough for a rotation turn inside the window: activation two days before the window ends may produce no appearance if his slot falls after it, whereas a position player activated the same day usually enters at once, so the same rehab stage implies different window probabilities by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare days from activation to first appearance for starters versus position players and relievers in injured-list returns since 2015.

nonlinearities.shape: Small base rate with threshold increase for day-to-day injuries
nonlinearities.why: Probability is near zero for healthy players and rises sharply with a recorded day-to-day designation, so a linear effect misses the regime.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function by stage with right-skewed durations
nonlinearities.why: Progress through rehab stages is discrete and the time to the next stage is skewed by setbacks, so timing is not smooth in elapsed days.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in number of games: 1 - prod(1 - p) saturates with exposure
nonlinearities.why: With many games available, additional games add little to P(at least one); with few games, each adds a lot.

nonlinearities.shape: Regime step at clinching or elimination date
nonlinearities.why: Rest policy changes discontinuously at the point stakes disappear.

mechanism_review.summary: Participation contracts depend on a manager's decision conditional on a player's availability. For a single game the chain is: roster status (active, injured list, minors), the manager's rest and platoon policy for that day (day game after night game, catcher rest, opposing starter handedness, DH rotation), posting of the lineup card a few hours before first pitch, and the residual chance of a late scratch between posting and the first pitch. Before the card posts the probability is a mixture over the manager's patterns, after it is near one unless the player is hurt in warm-up. For windows (will he pitch between two dates) availability is a hazard process: a returning player must progress through a rehab sequence, the team must have a role and a reason (race, rest of rotation), and injury risk can end it. For return windows (will an injured player appear for his club between two dates) the same rehab hazard applies, with the minor-league rehab assignment as the last observable stage and activation from the injured list as the trigger. The edge lies in knowing the timing of information (lineup posting relative to price) and in the specific manager and player, not in team strength.

stages.name: Roster status and health gate
stages.description: A player must be on the active roster and healthy; IL placement, minor-league assignment, rehab status and day-to-day injuries set the upper bound on the probability of any participation. Injury information arrives through official transactions and beat reports and is timestamped, so the information vintage determines the model state.
stages.distribution: Mostly 0/1 with an uncertain middle for day-to-day and returning players.

stages.name: Manager's decision for the specific game
stages.description: Given health, the manager decides to start the player based on role (everyday, platoon, bench), the opposing starter's handedness, rest patterns after travel or a night game, catcher and veteran rest conventions, DH rotation and lineup construction style, and in September or when clinched, rest and prospect-call-up policy. Players on a platoon sit against same-handed starters unless exceptions apply.
stages.distribution: Binary, with probabilities of start by role: everyday about 0.9, platoon 0.3-0.7 by opposing hand, bench near 0.1.

stages.name: Lineup posting and late-scratch hazard
stages.description: The lineup card is posted several hours before first pitch; the start market is effectively resolved then, except for the late-scratch hazard between posting and the first pitch (pregame injury, illness, warm-up). The market contract resolves No if the announced lineup changes before the game, so the late-scratch probability conditional on posting is a small but non-zero residual that depends on the player's injury status.
stages.distribution: Time-to-event: near-certain at card posting; residual probability of a scratch about 1-3% for listed starters, higher with day-to-day injuries.

stages.name: Window availability and exposure
stages.description: The pitch-in-window market integrates over games: the probability that a player records at least one pitch in a window is one minus the product of per-game non-appearance probabilities, but failures are strongly correlated through an absorbing injury state and through the team's plan, so a hazard model with injury absorption is appropriate. A rehabbing or two-way player needs a plan for pitching.
stages.distribution: Compound survival with absorption; per-game probabilities correlated; right-censored by season end.

stages.name: Return-from-injury window
stages.description: KXMLBRETURN asks whether an injured player enters any game for his named club inside a window. The chain is injury type and date, minimum injured-list duration, the rehab sequence (throwing or hitting progression, minor-league rehab assignment with its day limits), the club's activation decision given roster need and the race, and then the first game entry, which for a position player is almost immediate after activation and for a starting pitcher waits for a rotation turn. Setbacks reset the sequence, and a trade to another club would end exposure for the named club.
stages.distribution: Time-to-return with a long right tail by injury class (lognormal-like), discrete steps at rehab milestones, and a setback probability that creates a second mode well after the window.

stages.name: Starting-pitcher rotation slot
stages.description: The starting-pitcher market follows the rotation slot after off days, skipped starts, six-man or opener plans and staff injuries, with the announced probable replaced only occasionally (illness, short-notice injury, a bullpen game). It does not follow from the hitter lineup-card chain in stages s1-s3: the decision is made days earlier and announced as a probable, so the information vintage is the probable-pitcher announcement rather than the card.
stages.distribution: Near-deterministic once the slot is announced (P about 0.9 or higher) with a small change tail; before announcement a mixture over slot orderings driven by off days and rest.

role_personnel.note: Hitter role and platoon; pitcher rotation slot.

environment.note: Travel and day-night schedule.

game_context_script.note: Standings state affects rest in September.

pace_volume.note: Games in the window.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, congestion and clinched status. Regular-season construct: postseason has no clinch-rest and different roster rules (pp_postseason_regime).

settlement_contract.note: Official starting order, pinch hitter exclusion, window rules.

talent_strength.note: Player or team quality does not change whether a player starts except through role (starter versus bench), which is captured in the playing_time_role input; no talent estimate is needed beyond that for the participation event.

opponent_matchup.note: The opposing probable starter's identity and handedness drive platoon starts, but no input carries the opposing starter's identity or its announcement vintage, so platoon-driven start decisions are modelled without it (see pp_opp_starter_vintage).

efficiency_conversion.note: Participation has no conversion rate per opportunity; the closest object is the probability that a posted lineup holds, treated as a hazard in late_scratch_hazard.

distribution_variance.note: The outcome is binary (or at least one in a window); the relevant shape is the correlation of per-game failures through injury, captured in the window exposure and rehab inputs rather than a separate distribution variable.

officiating_rules.note: No officiating factor affects whether a player starts; only roster rules (active roster size, option and IL rules) matter, which are captured in settlement and roster-move inputs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Five live series after the reconciliation. KXMLBSTART (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player is in the official starting batting order (including as designated hitter) when the game begins; announcement in an earlier lineup then replacement before the game begins resolves No, and entering later as a pinch hitter or substitute does not qualify. KXMLBPITCH (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player records at least one pitch in a regular-season game inside a date window (example after Jul 28 and before Sep 28, 2026). KXMLBRETURN (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player 'must enter a game for the Tigers' (his named club) after one date and before another; it does not restrict the window to the regular season and is silent on a trade to another club. KXMLBSTARTER (starting pitcher) and KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP are title-only. CAUTION: the sampled KXMLBSTART rules_secondary is truncated at 'An actual plate appearance is ', so a clause that may require a plate appearance is unseen (pp_start_rules_truncated). Late insertion: a bench player placed into the posted card before the game begins because a teammate is scratched is in the official starting order when the game begins and resolves Yes; the No path applies only to the replaced player. Next-team and debut markets moved to transactions.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official starting batting order recorded by the league (MLB Stats API game feed) for start markets; league game logs for pitch and game-entry records (KXMLBPITCH, KXMLBRETURN); injured-list transactions for return timing.
variants_and_edge_cases: Population differs: single-game starting-lineup markets (KXMLBSTART, KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP), a starting-pitcher market (KXMLBSTARTER), a window-long 'will he pitch' market (KXMLBPITCH) and a window-long return market for an injured player with his named club (KXMLBRETURN) have different hazards (manager's lineup decision, rotation slot, injury/rehab progression).

Start market: an announced lineup that changes before first pitch resolves No (late scratch), so lineup posting time and warm-up scratch hazard matter; a player who starts as pitcher qualifies only if he is in the batting order.

Pitch window: regular season only (postseason pitches do not count in the sampled text), 'after' and 'before' dates are exclusive, and rehab appearances in the minors presumably do not count; exact handling of injury list is not stated.

KXMLBSTARTER is title-only: whether it settles on the announced probable or on the pitcher who throws the first pitch, and how an opener day is treated, is unseen; the hitter-card rule (announced then replaced resolves No) may not carry over.

Late card insertion: the player who replaces a scratched starter before first pitch settles Yes under 'official starting batting order ... when the game begins', so late_scratch_hazard for the replaced player and a late-insertion probability for bench players are two different quantities.

Return window (KXMLBRETURN): any entry into a game for the named club counts, including a pinch-running or relief appearance; the text names the club, so a trade before the return presumably resolves No, and unlike KXMLBPITCH it does not say 'regular season' (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, pp_return_scope).

announcer_mentions.label: Broadcast word-mention markets
announcer_mentions.target: Whether a specified word or phrase is spoken in the named broadcast, per the contract's source and counting rules.
announcer_mentions.mechanism: Mention probability reflects announcer vocabulary (crew-specific base rates), the length of the broadcast and events that trigger topics (milestones, pitching changes, weather delays, named players), with the contract's definition of which feed and what counts. Baseball statistics offer little direct signal, so this is closer to a novelty/language market with sparse history; the best hypotheses concern crew habits and trigger events.

inputs.why: Crew language tendencies and base word rates.
Which crew and network call the game.
Storylines and events that trigger words.
Recent storylines that announcers will discuss.
Delays add airtime and topics.
Longer games add airtime: extra innings require a tie after nine innings; the probability depends on expected run totals and spread.
Postseason broadcasts differ in language.
Which feed, speakers and spoken vs displayed words count.
Market-implied probability and movement.
Historical realised frequency by word type.
The market is a Poisson-like exposure market with crew-specific rates; without these the probability is unanchored.
Converts a per-hour word rate into a per-game probability.
Name-based markets are driven by involvement, not by baseball skill statistics.

CONDITIONAL on contract text: only relevant if a future contract counts ad reads or sponsor segments; otherwise exclude it. Separates the deterministic scripted part of language from spontaneous commentary and respects counting rules.

interactions.hypothesis: Crew vocabulary x trigger events: the word probability is the crew's baseline rate plus a bump when the trigger event occurs, so trigger-event likelihood should be modelled separately.
Broadcast length x word rate: delays and extra innings lengthen the broadcast, so game-length uncertainty interacts with word rate.
Wording x feed: national vs local feeds differ and the contract defines the counted feed, so crew identity interacts with rules text.

P(at least one mention) = 1 - exp(-rate x hours) saturates in exposure for common words but is nearly linear for rare ones, so extending airtime by extras or delays matters only for words whose rate times hours is below about two. Crew determines the rate that sets which regime applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(word) as function of crew-specific rate and airtime; compare to linear approximation for rare and common words.

interactions.hypothesis: Topical words occur at baseline until a trigger fires, after which the rate jumps; the market probability is the mixture P(trigger) x P(word|trigger) + (1-P(trigger)) x baseline. Scheduled triggers (milestone chase, rivalry games) are visible pregame, but in-game triggers (no-hitter, injury) are not.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition word frequency on trigger flags in transcripts and test mixture versus homogeneous rate.

interactions.hypothesis: National versus local feed and counting rules (sponsors, graphics) switch the effective vocabulary; a contract limited to the national feed uses a different crew and sponsor mix than the home feed, so probability is determined first by the regime then by the rate. This holds only if a contract that counts ad reads exists (none in the ledger); treat as conditional.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate word rates separately by feed type and counting rule version; compare out-of-sample calibration.

interactions.hypothesis: A player's name rate multiplies his involvement (PA, pitching) and the storyline salience (return from injury, award talk); a star in a storyline gets a rate several times a bench player's, and a non-starter gets zero, so involvement gates the storyline effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit mention-rate model with involvement x storyline interaction on transcripts.

interactions.hypothesis: Delays and extras both lengthen the broadcast but are nearly independent events with different tails; the airtime distribution is a convolution with a heavy right tail, so rare-word probabilities have a fat contribution from long-game scenarios.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate airtime from separate delay and extras processes and check the correlation with game duration data.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: P(word) = 1 - E[(1+lambda*t/phi)^(-phi)] (negative-binomial zero probability), not the Poisson 1-exp(-lambda*t)
nonlinearities.why: Each additional minute adds less once the word has a high chance of already having occurred. Dispersion-adjusted: clustering of topical words means the Poisson form overstates P(at least one) for the same mean rate; phi is estimated per word class.

nonlinearities.shape: Overdispersion with zero inflation: P(0) far above Poisson for topical words
nonlinearities.why: Clustering and topic persistence make many games have none and a few have many, which changes P(at least one).

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold: probability jumps once the trigger occurs (no-hitter after the 6th inning, milestone in sight)
nonlinearities.why: Topical language is gated by event occurrence, producing a step in rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in PA but jump in high-leverage PA or milestones
nonlinearities.why: Name frequency scales with action, with additional jumps in salient moments.

mechanism_review.summary: A word-mention market is a count of spoken occurrences in an exposure window, settled Yes if the count is at least one. The generating process is a point process: each crew has a baseline per-hour rate for each word, shaped by its vocabulary and by the broadcast format (national versus local, play-by-play versus color), multiplied by the length of the broadcast (nine innings take about two and a half to three hours, extras and delays extend it), plus event-triggered bursts when game events make the word relevant (a no-hitter in progress, a milestone, weather, injuries, the name of a player who comes to bat). Baseball statistics offer weak direct signal; most of the information is which crew is on the air, what the game script will produce, and who the players of interest are. Occurrences cluster because topics persist, so counts are overdispersed and the probability of at least one is lower than the Poisson at the same mean for low-rate words and higher for topic-driven words. Little structured data exists, so the quality of any prior depends on building transcripts.

stages.name: Which broadcast and crew
stages.description: The contract names a broadcast; its crew (play-by-play announcer, color analyst, sideline reporter), network (national such as Fox, ESPN, TBS, or the local regional network) and language determine the vocabulary and the style. National postseason crews differ from local crews in word choice, in discussion of rivalry and in sponsor language. The same game can have different feeds with very different base rates.
stages.distribution: Categorical crew identity with heterogeneous base-rate distributions; crew changes (injury or schedule) rare but discrete.

stages.name: Exposure time
stages.description: The window is the broadcast, which runs from first pitch to the final out plus any specified pre- and post-game segments; time depends on pace of play, pitching changes, extras and weather delays. Exposure is random: a seven-inning game or a delayed game changes the available time by tens of minutes, and a game called early shortens it.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed duration (about 2.4 to 3.2 hours typical; delays add up to hours); extras add about 15-20 minutes per inning.

stages.name: Word base rate per crew
stages.description: Given exposure, the count of a specific word follows a point process with a crew-specific rate per hour; common baseball words are near-certain to occur, while rare or topical words have rates below one per game. Rates differ by crew because of verbal habits (frequent use of 'Statcast', specific player nicknames, sponsor read phrases).
stages.distribution: Poisson-like with overdispersion; zero-inflated for rare words; per-crew rate heterogeneity.

stages.name: Triggered topics and named entities
stages.description: Words referring to events or people occur only when the game or the news makes them relevant: a pitcher's perfect game attempt, a milestone, a player returning from injury, a trade, weather, an umpire dispute, a rivalry. Names of players are used in proportion to their involvement (plate appearances, pitching) and storylines. These are bursts above the base rate with probabilities that depend on game events and pregame narratives.
stages.distribution: Event-triggered bursts: probability of word given trigger is high, trigger probability low; mixture structure.

stages.name: Counting rules and clustering
stages.description: What counts (inflections, spoken versus displayed, ads) changes the effective exposure and rate; counts cluster because once a topic is introduced it is repeated, so the distribution is overdispersed and the probability of at least one relative to the mean is shape-dependent. The settlement resolver's counting also introduces measurement noise.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed (negative-binomial or self-exciting) count; P(count >= 1) depends on dispersion parameter and zero mass.

variants_and_edge_cases: Feed ambiguity: a national telecast, a regional sports network home feed and an away feed have different crews and vocabularies; the contract's named source decides which crew's language rate applies.

transactions.label: Transactions, coaching and personnel events
transactions.target: Whether a trade, signing, call-up, extension or manager/coach change occurs by a given date.
transactions.mechanism: Transactions follow institutional calendars and team incentives: standing (buyer vs seller), contract status, roster-rule constraints and front-office behaviour, with beat-writer reports preceding many official moves. The probability is a hazard over the contract window, estimated from reference classes and updated by reports and standings, with the resolution defined by official announcement.

inputs.why: Transaction timeline and rules.
Team standing drives trade behaviour.
Option, 40-man and Rule 5 constraints.
Reports precede transactions: transactions and news change who plays and the team's strength with a lag before statistics catch up.
Injuries trigger call-ups and IL moves.
Playoff odds define buyer/seller state.
Reference-class frequencies: for off-field markets, history of similar announcements is the best available prior.
What counts as an official transaction.
Market reaction to reports: the traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
Defines feasibility and timing, which are first-order for next-team markets.
Provides the likelihood ratio for the most important information type.
Gives time-conditioned base rates instead of one reference-class rate.
Explains who can sign or trade for salary and so conditions signing and trade probabilities.
The vacancy hazard is the first stage of next-manager contracts.
Adds the selection stage the record lacked: the markets are one-per-team and one-per-candidate.
Adds the missing labour-stoppage regime for transactions whose windows span Dec 1 2026.

Defined here while KXMLBDRAFTPICK was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation that series is in the amateur-draft archetype, which has no review yet; kept so the definition is not lost, not staged here.

interactions.hypothesis: Playoff odds x contract status: sellers with expiring contracts are most likely traded, so standing and contract status interact for trade probability.
Rule calendar x report timing: option/40-man deadlines concentrate moves on specific dates, so hazards should be date-aware and reports tighten the window.
Report credibility x price reaction: price changes after reports measure their credibility and the rules define whether they count.

A seller with an expiring contract in the final weeks before the deadline has a trade hazard that is the product of team status (seller), player contract (expiring, tradable) and calendar proximity, so none of these alone predicts a trade; each multiplies the daily hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit Cox hazard with interaction of seller status, expiring contract and days to deadline.

interactions.hypothesis: The completion probability given a report depends on wording and source, and on whether the rules count only the official announcement; a credible 'pending physical' report implies high probability of completion within days but not certainty. The official-versus-report distinction is an assumption about settlement until the full rules are read.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate completion probability by source-wording class and time since report.

interactions.hypothesis: Payroll headroom acts as a threshold: teams near the tax line are very unlikely to add salary beyond it, so a free-agent signing probability for that team is near zero until headroom exceeds the contract's annual value; contract structure shifts the effective threshold.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate signing probability by headroom to AAV ratio and test discontinuity near zero headroom.

interactions.hypothesis: Managers are fired in-season mainly when the team is out of contention, and in the offseason after the season ends; the hazard regime switches at the end of the season, and the next-manager market depends on a vacancy created in the first regime or second.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard in regular season versus offseason and test dependence on playoff odds.

interactions.hypothesis: Injury-driven call-ups and IL moves are constrained by roster and option rules, so the number of available call-up slots and the date relative to roster expansions changes the hazard in steps.
interactions.how_to_test: Segment history by roster-rule regime and compare call-up rates.

interactions.hypothesis: During a lockout the signing hazard is zero and the destination choice cannot resolve; after an agreement the pent-up signings arrive in a rush on compressed calendar anchors, so the probability a named destination wins before March 25 2027 equals P(lockout ends in time) times the post-deal destination share.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare March 2022 signing rate and destination shares with the pre-lockout December 2021 rush and with ordinary years.

interactions.hypothesis: On deadline day many agreements are reported in the final hour, and the trade market counts only those officially processed before the date; a credible report of an agreed deal minutes before the deadline converts to Yes only if processing lands in time, and players with no-trade or 10-and-5 rights add a consent step that can push completion past the cutoff.
interactions.how_to_test: For deadline-day trades since 2015, compare report timestamps with official processing times and estimate the share of late-reported deals that miss the cutoff, split by no-trade status.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise-constant spikes at calendar anchors
nonlinearities.why: Events cluster around fixed dates, so cumulative probability over a window is a step-like function of window placement.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in playoff odds (illustrative author guess near 10-20%, to be estimated) where teams flip from buyers to sellers
nonlinearities.why: Teams behave discontinuously around the contention boundary, so a linear function of playoff odds misprices behaviour.

nonlinearities.shape: Beta-posterior shrinkage with source report count
nonlinearities.why: Reliability is estimated from few reports per source, so posterior probability depends nonlinearly on counts.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at zero headroom
nonlinearities.why: Teams avoid crossing tax lines, so signing probability collapses near and below zero headroom.

mechanism_review.summary: Transactions follow institutional calendars and incentives, so the event is a time-to-event process with hazards that change by date and context. For trades, a seller with a short-contract player is likely to deal near the deadline and the buyer-seller status of the team is driven by playoff probability and payroll; for free-agent signings, contract expiry, qualifying-offer decisions, positional market and team payroll space drive timing, with most signings clustered in the first weeks of free agency and again at the winter meetings; for manager changes, tenure, team underperformance relative to expectations, owner statements and contract status matter. Beat-writer reports precede most official moves, with source credibility varying; the contract resolves on the official announcement, so lead times and process failures (physicals, vetoes) matter. There is little statistical structure in team performance beyond its effect on incentives, so the best-supported approach is reference-class hazard modelling updated by timestamped reports. The trade market (KXMLBTRADE) settles on official MLB processing before the date and ignores later rescissions, so the relevant process ends at league approval, not at a physical. After the reconciliation the archetype also holds the prospect-debut market, a hazard over the call-up pipeline, and a next-manager market; the draft-pick market moved to its own archetype.

stages.name: Eligibility and constraints
stages.description: A transaction requires that the player or manager is eligible: contract expiry or opt-out for free agency, service time and 40-man status for call-ups and trades, no-trade protections and 10-and-5 rights, club options, and the qualifying offer system. The constraint set determines which events are possible at all and when.
stages.distribution: Binary feasibility gating with time-varying eligibility dates.

stages.name: Team incentives and finances
stages.description: Buyer or seller status depends on playoff probability and distance to contention; payroll and luxury-tax thresholds constrain the ability to add salary; managers are fired when expectations are missed and the organization is willing to pay a replacement. Incentives are partly observable from standings and projections.
stages.distribution: Continuous incentive index with threshold behaviour at playoff-odds boundaries.

stages.name: Calendar and process timing
stages.description: Transaction hazards are not constant: trade deadline day, the end-of-season window, the non-tender and qualifying-offer deadlines, the winter meetings, the Rule 5 draft and the start of spring training concentrate events on known dates. Process steps (negotiation, medical review, league processing) add lags between agreement and official processing; for the trade market only processing before the date counts, so deadline-day agreements processed late are the boundary cases.
stages.distribution: Piecewise-constant hazard with spikes at calendar anchors; lag distribution from agreement to official.

stages.name: Information flow and report credibility
stages.description: Credible reporters often announce agreements hours or days before official announcements; the probability of eventual official completion given a report depends on the report's wording ('close to', 'agreed', 'pending physical') and on the reporter's track record. Prices respond to reports, so the quantity of interest is the posterior given report text and source.
stages.distribution: Bayesian update with source-specific likelihood ratios; most information arrives in discrete jumps.

stages.name: Resolution wording and failure modes
stages.description: Contracts resolve on events meeting specified conditions, and the wording differs by series: a trade counts once officially processed and approved by MLB before the date and stays Yes even if later rescinded or voided by a failed physical, whereas the next-team text is silent on announcement, physicals and voiding. Remaining failure modes before official processing include a collapsed negotiation, a player using no-trade rights, a sign-and-trade, or processing that lands after the market date.
stages.distribution: Absorbing event with a small pre-processing failure mass after a report; zero post-processing failure mass for trades by rule; wording determines edge cases.

stages.name: Destination or candidate selection and labour regime
stages.description: After eligibility and timing, a free agent chooses among teams and a club chooses among manager candidates, so the market object is a categorical choice shaped by positional need, competing bids, market size and preferences; independently, a CBA lockout beginning after Dec 1 2026 would freeze transactions for an unknown time, making any window that spans the expiry a mixture over stoppage length.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice with a few credible destinations and a long tail; stoppage length is a heavy-tailed mixture with zero-length (no lockout) mass.

stages.name: Debut and next-manager events
stages.description: A debut before a multi-year deadline is a hazard over the call-up pipeline (40-man status, options, minor-league performance, positional need and service-time incentives), not a lineup decision; any club counts, so a trade does not reset it. The next-manager market first needs a vacancy, which depends on the incumbent's firing hazard (tenure, underperformance versus expectation, contract status), and then is a selection among named candidates driven by interview reports and front-office ties.
stages.distribution: Debut: right-skewed time-to-event with spikes at September and injury call-ups and near-certain mass for top prospects; manager: vacancy hazard followed by a categorical choice with a front-runner.

talent_strength.note: Team strength through playoff odds.

role_personnel.note: Contract and eligibility, call-up pipeline and manager candidate selection.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Incentives, calendar and finance.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed stage durations and a lockout mixture; the weak all-family base rate is no longer claimed.

settlement_contract.note: Official processing before the date for trades (rescission after processing still Yes), status-quo and re-signing clauses for next team, any-club debut definition.

opponent_matchup.note: Competing bidders and positional need decide which team signs the player.

environment.note: Venue, weather and altitude do not affect transaction timing; location of a team may affect free agent preferences only weakly and is not measurable in a way a market can price.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume of opportunities in a transaction event; the quantity analogous to pace is the calendar hazard rate, included under calendar timing.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate per opportunity applies; the nearest object is the stage conversion from report to official announcement, included as report credibility.

officiating_rules.note: CBA windows, lockout freezes and service-time rules are the rule regime of transactions.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four live series after the reconciliation. KXMLBTRADE (rules sampled): Yes if the named player is traded before the date; 'The trade must be officially processed and approved by MLB' before the date, and a trade later rescinded or voided by a failed physical after official processing still resolves Yes. KXMLBNEXTTEAM (rules sampled): one market per team plus 'Retires / No Team'; a player who remains on his issuance team on the date resolves for that team, a free agent who 'signs a contract with any team, including their previous team' resolves for that team, an extension or re-signing while under contract does not trigger early resolution, and retirement or no team on the date resolves Retires/No Team (text truncated after that). KXMLBDEBUT (rules sampled): Yes if the named prospect 'plays for any MLB team in a regular season or playoff game' before the date (Nov 1, 2028 in the sample); what counts as playing (pinch-running, defensive replacement) is not defined. KXMLBCOACH (next manager) is title-only. The draft-pick market moved to the amateur-draft archetype. Whether NEXTTEAM waits for an official announcement, and how a failed physical affects a signing, is not stated (see tr_settlement_assumed).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official team or league transaction announcements (MLB transactions log); not named in the sampled rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: Next-team: a player who stays with his team resolves Yes for that team at the date, a free agent who signs elsewhere resolves for the new team; extensions while under contract do not resolve early.

Announcement and physicals: for trades the text requires official MLB processing before the date and keeps a Yes even if the trade is later rescinded or a physical is failed; for NEXTTEAM the text says only 'signs a contract with any team' and is silent on announcement, physicals or voiding, so the trade rule cannot be assumed to carry over (see tr_settlement_assumed).
Manager markets: the next manager of a team requires a hire announcement, and interim managers are an edge case not covered in the sample.
Deadline structure: trade-deadline, non-tender, qualifying offer and Rule 5 dates create calendar clusters where the market window includes or excludes them.
Debut: the window spans more than two seasons and any club counts, so a trade does not reset the clock; whether a pinch-running or defensive-only appearance counts as 'plays' is undefined.

Trade window (KXMLBTRADE): the sampled date (Aug 5, 2026) presumably falls just after the 2026 trade deadline (deadline date not verified here), so nearly all mass would sit in deadline week; no-trade clauses, 10-and-5 rights and club control years shape feasibility, and processing lag on deadline day decides borderline cases.

offfield_markets.label: Business, non-baseball and esports novelty markets
offfield_markets.target: Events outside baseball games settled by public announcement or defined sources.
offfield_markets.mechanism: These markets are driven by organisational decisions and external events rather than on-field performance. There is little statistical structure: the best-supported hypotheses are reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints and timestamped news relative to the resolution wording. Non-baseball and esports items are not predicted by baseball inputs at all and should be treated as novelty markets with no baseball model.

inputs.why: Reference-class frequency: for off-field markets, history of similar announcements is the best available prior.
Timestamped reports: transactions and news change who plays and the team's strength with a lag before statistics catch up.
Transaction calendar where relevant.
Resolution wording and source.
Price reaction to news: the traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
Liquidity affects quote reliability.
Close time vs event timing: market open, close, halts and postponement events determine when information can be traded on and which pregame snapshot is the last valid one.
Other venues' prices where they exist.
Base rates by market type: realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
Gives a concrete quantity for the voter model rather than a generic base rate.
KXMLBTEAMSALE settles only on finalization and approval, so stage and duration drive the probability.
Provides the only relevant information for the esports contract and keeps baseball features from contaminating it.
Gives KXMLBCOACH an identity-level selection input; without it the series had no mechanism beyond a generic hazard.
KXMLBFODTEAMS resolves all clubs No if no 2027 game is announced with participants or played, so staging is the first multiplier.
Gives each KXMLBFODTEAMS club market a probability that respects the two-participant constraint and regional selection pattern.

interactions.hypothesis: Base rate x time remaining: hazard concentrates around known dates, so base rates must be time-conditioned by the market window.
News timing x resolution source: reports precede official announcements, so price reaction must be read against what the rules count.
Thin liquidity x price moves: sparse trading makes quotes noisy, so volume interacts with moves to separate information from noise.

A club's Yes probability is P(game staged) times its marginal in the pair choice; news that strengthens one club's selection does nothing if the event itself is doubtful, and a staging confirmation lifts every plausible club at once while leaving their ratios unchanged.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose historical special-event club probabilities into staging and selection parts and check that staging news moves club prices proportionally.

interactions.hypothesis: Under a lockout after Dec 1 2026 the 2027 schedule is not finalised, so selection cannot be announced and the event may be dropped; if the market closes before a delayed release the all-No branch applies, so labour risk matters more the earlier the close date.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare schedule-release dates in labour-dispute years (1994-95, 2021-22) with normal years and map them against the market close time.

interactions.hypothesis: A report naming a pairing moves club probabilities in proportion to the outlet's reliability for schedule leaks; local reports about hotel blocks or permits for specific dates are informative only if the clubs scheduled that week match the leaked pairing.
interactions.how_to_test: Score past schedule-leak reports by outlet against released schedules and fit outlet-level likelihood ratios.

interactions.hypothesis: Clubs beyond a few hundred miles of eastern Iowa have near-zero selection probability unless they are a national draw, so the distance effect is a threshold rather than a smooth decline, and the generic off-field base rate overstates distant clubs.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot selection frequency against distance for regional special events and test a threshold against a log-linear distance term.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in time at announcement dates
nonlinearities.why: Staging probability jumps to near one at the participant announcement and to near zero if the schedule is released without the event; between announcements it drifts only with venue and labour news.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in distance with a national-draw exception
nonlinearities.why: Selection mass falls sharply beyond driving distance of the site, except for a few national-draw clubs paired with a regional club, so a linear distance effect misprices both groups.

mechanism_review.summary: The Field of Dreams team market is a scheduling decision, not a sporting outcome. First the league must decide to stage a game at the Dyersville, Iowa site in 2027, which depends on venue readiness and its owners' development plans, the broadcast partner's appetite, the schedule-making calendar and, this cycle, a collective bargaining agreement that expires on Dec 1 2026 and could delay the 2027 schedule. Given a game, two clubs are chosen: the league and broadcaster favour Midwestern clubs within driving distance of Iowa, high-profile or nationally marketable matchups, clubs not used recently (2021 White Sox-Yankees, 2022 Cubs-Reds), and a designated home club willing to give up a home date at a stadium of roughly 8,000 seats; the pairing must fit the schedule matrix, usually as part of an existing series. The announcement normally arrives with the schedule release or in a dedicated press event, preceded by leaks of uneven credibility. Team quality and player performance play no role.

stages.name: Contract scope and resolution trigger
stages.description: The family must be identified from the rules text rather than the prefix, which has carried award, delay, esports, hiring and sale markets. For KXMLBFODTEAMS the text fixes a resolution trigger at team selection, an all-No branch if no 2027 game is announced with participants or played, and no explicit announcement deadline; the market close time relative to the expected schedule release decides how much labour-delay risk the contract carries.
stages.distribution: Deterministic routing; a small discrete probability that re-selection or a late announcement is treated differently from the plain reading.

stages.name: Whether a 2027 game is staged
stages.description: The league staged the game in 2021 and 2022 and skipped it from 2023 through 2025 while the Dyersville site was redeveloped, so staging is an annual decision driven by venue status, broadcast and sponsorship commitments, the league's portfolio of special-event games (Little League Classic, Rickwood, international series) and the schedule calendar. A lockout after the CBA expiry would delay the 2027 schedule and could remove the event entirely, which sends every club market to No.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with a probability that moves in jumps on venue, broadcaster and labour news; heavy dependence on a single league decision, so no averaging across clubs.

stages.name: Choice of the two participating clubs
stages.description: Given a game, the pair is chosen to maximise attendance draw, television value and regional fit: clubs within a few hundred miles of eastern Iowa (Cubs, White Sox, Cardinals, Twins, Royals, Brewers, Reds) carry most of the mass, a national draw can be paired with a regional club, recently used clubs are less likely, and the designated home club gives up a home date and gate revenue. The pairing must also exist in the 2027 schedule matrix (a division, rivalry or interleague series in mid-season).
stages.distribution: Categorical over about 435 unordered club pairs, concentrated on a few dozen Midwestern pairings; club-level marginals sum to two given staging, with strong negative dependence between clubs in the same slot.

stages.name: Schedule release and report flow
stages.description: Participants are usually confirmed with the schedule release or a dedicated announcement, and local reports, permit filings and broadcaster leaks precede it. Before the release the state is a posterior over staging and pairings given these reports weighted by source reliability; a CBA negotiation that delays the schedule shifts the announcement date and can push it past the market's close.
stages.distribution: Discrete jumps at report times; an announcement-date distribution that is right-skewed under labour uncertainty.

talent_strength.note: Club quality does not decide Field of Dreams participation; selection rests on geography, marketability and scheduling, so no team-strength input changes the club probabilities.

opponent_matchup.note: Which pairings are attractive (regional rivalry, national draw paired with a Midwestern club) and fit the schedule matrix.

role_personnel.note: The designated home club's willingness to give up a home date is the only club-role element; no player role matters.

availability_news.note: Timestamped leaks and announcements about staging and participants, scored by source reliability.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers and tactics have no influence on whether a club is chosen for a special-event game; the decision sits with the league office, the broadcaster and the clubs' business side.

environment.note: Venue readiness and status of the Dyersville site enter through the staging probability.

game_context_script.note: The contract resolves on selection, before any game is played, so no in-game state, score or leverage can affect it.

pace_volume.note: There are no opportunity counts; the only count is two participants per staged game, which is a structural constraint inside the pair-choice input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion exists; the event is a single league scheduling decision followed by a pair choice, with no repeated trials to convert.

distribution_variance.note: All club outcomes share one staging Bernoulli and a pair constraint, so outcomes are strongly dependent; few historical events make the base rate wide.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Event calendar, CBA expiry and schedule-matrix fit.

officiating_rules.note: The labour agreement governs whether and when the 2027 schedule is made; no on-field officiating applies.

settlement_contract.note: Selection trigger, all-No branch, missing deadline and market close relative to the schedule release.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Announcement date as first published; later changes recorded with their own dates.

candidate_sources.note: Official announcements of events and participants

required_data.grain: one row per club; one row per scheduled series
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Schedule matrix as released (or projected) at the as-of date.
required_data.history_needed: Current season plus matrices for the stagings used in fitting

fields: claim (staging, pairing, schedule date, CBA status)
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Publication timestamp; stored at capture.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Rules versioned at issuance.

contract_review.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation the only live series is KXMLBFODTEAMS (rules sampled): one market per club, Yes 'If Washington is confirmed to be in the Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game'; the market 'resolves immediately on team selection for the game', and 'If no Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game is announced to have participants or occurs, all markets resolve to No'. Two clubs are selected, so Yes probabilities across clubs sum to about two when a game is staged. The text gives no deadline for the announcement, does not say what happens if announced teams are later replaced or the game is cancelled after selection, and names no source beyond confirmation. The franchise-sale market formerly filed here (KXMLBTEAMSALE) was classified out of scope (franchise business); awards, delay and hiring series moved earlier.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official MLB schedule release and club announcements of the Field of Dreams participants (presumed); the text says only 'confirmed'.
variants_and_edge_cases: Two participants per game: club markets are a structured set whose Yes probabilities sum to two times P(game staged), so club probabilities must be modelled jointly as a pair choice rather than independently.

Selection precedes play: 'resolves immediately on team selection' means a club announced and later replaced (in 2020 the game was announced, re-planned and then cancelled before being played in 2021) would already have resolved Yes; the text does not address re-selection (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, off_reselection).

No deadline is stated for 'announced to have participants or occurs'; with the CBA expiring Dec 1 2026, a delayed 2027 schedule release postpones selection, and the market's close date governs whether a late announcement counts (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, off_no_deadline).
The event has been intermittent (played 2021 and 2022, not staged 2023-2025), so whether a 2027 game exists at all is the largest single factor, ahead of which clubs play.

player_and_team_counting_specials.label: MLB player/team counting specials (stolen bases, walks, outs recorded, earned runs, next home run)
player_and_team_counting_specials.target: A counting stat for a player or team over a game or season relative to a threshold, or which player does an event next.
player_and_team_counting_specials.mechanism: Counts are plate appearances (or batters faced) times per-PA probabilities with matchup adjustments; stolen bases add catcher and pitcher hold-time effects, walks add umpire zone and plate discipline, outs recorded depends on the starter's hook. Season-level counts add playing-time and availability risk.

inputs.why: Plate appearances by slot and script.
Walk rate depends on the hitter's patience and the pitcher's control; both set the per-PA walk probability.
Steal attempt rate, pitcher hold time and catcher arm.
Sprint speed and baserunning aggressiveness set the steal attempt rate and success probability.
Expected innings and batters faced.
Manager hook rules (pitch counts, times through the order) determine how many outs the starter records.
The run-scoring distribution gives the tail probabilities for earned runs and team-count thresholds.
Bullpen availability decides outs after the starter.
Confirmed batting order timestamped.
Starter versus platoon role sets plate appearances and games played over a season.
Umpire strike-zone size changes walk and strikeout rates and therefore walks and outs recorded.
PA simulation gives count distributions.
Provides a calculation for the whole family of season-extreme markets that existing inputs do not cover.
The sampled contract is exactly this joint threshold, with regular-season counting only.
Gives the extreme-value measurement for the velocity markets.
KXMLBSERIESSCORE settles on exact score and needs the full distribution.
Prices the streak contracts using the right object (extremes) instead of inning mechanics.
Replaces the 'wording error' diagnosis for SEASONGAMES and OPENINGDAY with an explicit stoppage scenario model.
Defines the actual required inputs for team extremes (previously only an engine and an unresolved gap).
Gives KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS a defined input; without it the series had no mechanism after moving into this archetype.
Gives KXMLBSISTREAK its outcome-generating process: per-out survival over the outs still needed within the starts left.

interactions.hypothesis: A speedster's steal probability depends on batting slot and the hitters behind him.
A tight zone inflates walks most for patient hitters.
Outs recorded is the starter's pitch efficiency times the hook rule.

Walk-offs need games, and only games that reach the home team's last at-bat tied or narrowly behind; the count is therefore games remaining (set by bracket path and series length) times a per-game rate that rises with evenly matched, low-scoring pairings. A long series between two strong pitching staffs raises both factors at once, so the two cannot be estimated separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress postseason walk-offs per game on pre-game total and win-probability gap, and compare count calibration with and without path-dependent games remaining.

interactions.hypothesis: The playoff HR total is a compound sum: its variance is the variance of the number of games times the squared per-game mean plus the per-game dispersion times the expected games. Early in October the games-remaining term dominates and the threshold probability moves in steps with each series result; late, per-game park and weather matter more.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose the variance of simulated playoff HR totals into games-count and per-game parts by date and compare with realised totals 2015-2025.

interactions.hypothesis: A 2+ series home-run rung needs two events, so its probability rises faster than linearly in total plate appearances: a series that goes seven games instead of four nearly doubles a hitter's chances for 1+ but more than triples them for 2+, and the effect is larger for high per-PA power rates.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised series home-run rungs against a linear-in-games model, split by series length and hitter power tier.

interactions.hypothesis: In the date-window market a healthy power hitter's probability saturates quickly (he usually homers within a few weeks), so almost all uncertainty is the injury state: a hitter on the injured list with an uncertain return has a probability governed by return timing, not power.
interactions.how_to_test: Split historical windows by injured-list status at the as-of date and compare realised hit rates with the power-only model.

interactions.hypothesis: A streak can only reach N if enough starts remain to record the needed outs: late in the season the rung becomes impossible once remaining starts times outs per start falls below the gap, regardless of how dominant the pitcher is.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the maximum attainable streak from remaining starts and check that market rungs beyond it settle No.

interactions.hypothesis: Runners a streaking pitcher leaves on base and who later score are charged to him and, if the streak counts all charged runs, break it; managers protecting a streak pull him with bases empty, so the bullpen and exit-state policy change survival late in starts.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical long streaks, compare the share of streak-ending runs scored by inherited runners with the share expected from typical exit states.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function in time as series end; convex in games remaining for a 5+ threshold
nonlinearities.why: A threshold of several walk-offs needs many close games; each finished series removes potential games in a step, and the probability of reaching N rises faster than linearly with remaining games because several rare events must coincide.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in outs needed
nonlinearities.why: Each inning survives with probability q, so P(reach N) is about q to the power of the innings needed; a change in q from 0.78 to 0.82 nearly doubles the chance of a ten-inning gap.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in plate appearances for 2+ rungs
nonlinearities.why: Two home runs are needed, so the rung grows roughly with the square of exposure at low rates; series length and benching change it more than proportionally.

mechanism_review.summary: After the reconciliation this unregistered bucket holds three mechanisms. Postseason league counts (walk-offs, total home runs) are sums over a random number of playoff games: the number of games comes from the bracket and series lengths, each game contributes a walk-off with a probability set by close-late game states and the home team's last at-bat, and home runs per game come from the two lineups, parks and October weather. Player home-run exposure markets (series total, home run inside a date window) are the hitter's per-plate-appearance home-run rate times his plate appearances, where plate appearances depend on how many games the series lasts or how many games fall in the window and whether he plays them; injury acts as an absorbing state and the count is convex in exposure for 2+ rungs. The pitcher scoreless-innings streak is a survival process over outs: each out recorded without a run charged extends the streak by a third of an inning, and the streak ends at the first run charged, so the probability of reaching N innings is a product of per-out survival over the outs still needed, limited by the starts remaining before the season ends.

stages.name: Contract family classification and gate
stages.description: Five series span postseason league counts, player home-run exposure markets and a pitcher scoreless streak. Routing from the rules text comes first because the exposure window (all playoff games, one series, a date window, or until the streak breaks or the season ends), the counted event (any walk-off despite a home-run title; scoreless outs at one third of an inning) and the nested-rung settlement differ by series and change what is priced.
stages.distribution: Categorical routing; window and event definitions change the payout function, not the underlying process.

stages.name: Postseason event counts over a random number of games
stages.description: Playoff walk-offs and playoff home runs are sums over every playoff game, so their exposure is the number of games, which depends on series lengths and how many rounds are left. Each game produces a walk-off only when the home team is tied or trailing narrowly entering its last at-bat and then takes the lead, which depends on close-game frequency and the visiting closer; home runs per game depend on the two lineups, parks and October weather. Counts so far are known, so late in the playoffs the market is a short remaining-games problem.
stages.distribution: Walk-offs: Poisson-binomial over remaining games (per-game probability a few percent) mixed over the games-remaining distribution; home runs: negative-binomial per game with game-shared dispersion, summed over a random number of games.

stages.name: Player home runs across one playoff series
stages.description: A named hitter's series home-run total is the sum over the series' games of his home runs, so it depends on how many games the series lasts (four to seven in a best-of-seven), whether he starts each one, his plate appearances per game and his per-PA home-run rate against the specific rotation he will face, adjusted for the two parks and October weather. There is no start gate, so a benched or injured hitter accrues fewer chances rather than voiding.
stages.distribution: Compound sum over a random number of games of per-game Poisson-binomial counts; P(2+) is convex in total plate appearances and sensitive to series length.

stages.name: Player home run inside a date window
stages.description: KXMLBNEXTHR pays if the hitter homers in any MLB game inside the window, so the probability is one minus the product over scheduled games of the per-game no-home-run probability, where each game's chance depends on whether he plays, his plate appearances and his per-PA rate. Injury is an absorbing state that ends exposure until his return, so the injured-list status and rehab timeline at the as-of date dominate for a hurt player; a trade keeps exposure because any MLB game counts.
stages.distribution: Survival in games with per-game hazard around 0.10-0.25 for regular power hitters; mixture over an injury state with long absences; right-censored at the window end.

stages.name: Scoreless-innings streak survival
stages.description: From the current streak length, reaching N innings requires 3*(N - current) further consecutive outs with no run charged to the pitcher. Per-out survival comes from his run-prevention profile (strikeouts, walks, home runs and sequencing), the opponents and parks of his next starts, and the chance that runners he leaves on base score after he exits. The number of starts left before the regular season ends caps the outs available, and an injured-list stint pauses exposure.
stages.distribution: Approximately geometric in innings (per-inning scoreless probability around 0.70-0.85 for elite starters), so P(reach N) decays exponentially in outs needed; truncated by remaining starts.

talent_strength.note: Hitter power profile for series and window home runs; pitcher run prevention for the streak.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing rotation HR vulnerability in a series, the visiting closer in walk-off states, lineup-versus-pitcher HR rates per playoff game.

role_personnel.note: Whether the hitter starts the games in his window or series; the pitcher's rotation slot and remaining starts.

availability_news.note: Injury absorbs exposure in the window and series markets and pauses a streak.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager tactics matter only through bullpen deployment in close late games, the hook decision for a streaking starter and lineup choices, all carried by bullpen, inherited-runner and playing-time inputs.

environment.note: Parks and weather of the series games scale per-PA home-run rates.

game_context_script.note: Close-and-late game states that create walk-offs.

pace_volume.note: Playoff games remaining, series length, games in the window and outs per start.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-out probability of avoiding a charged run and conversion of baserunners to runs.

distribution_variance.note: Compound playoff counts, convex series totals and geometric streak survival.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Off days and doubleheaders in the window; starts remaining before season end for the streak.

officiating_rules.note: Umpires do not move these counts at first order; official scoring of inside-the-park home runs and of earned runs is a settlement-definition issue handled under settlement_contract.

settlement_contract.note: Exposure windows, walk-off definition, one-third-inning streak credit and nested rungs.
