contract_review.settlement_definition: Five live series after the reconciliation, all with sampled rules. Postseason league counts: KXMLBWALKOFFS (at least N walk-offs in the 2026 playoffs; 'A walk-off occurs when a game ends with the home team scoring the winning run in the bottom half of the 9th inning or any extra inning', however the run scores) and KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS (at least N home runs by all players in the 2026 playoffs, inside-the-park counted if officially recorded). Player home runs: KXMLBSERIESHR (named player's officially recorded home runs across one playoff series, extra innings and inside-the-park included, other rounds excluded; no start gate) and KXMLBNEXTHR (Yes if the named player 'hits a home run in an MLB game' after one date and before another, No otherwise). Pitcher streak: KXMLBSISTREAK (Yes if the named pitcher reaches N consecutive scoreless innings from the stated streak start until the streak ends or the regular season concludes; partial innings count 1/3 per scoreless out; a broken streak resolves unreached rungs No). No text names a source, and none defines what breaks a streak (earned versus unearned runs, inherited runners) or how a player who misses games settles. Season team extremes, velocity and series exact-score markets moved to season_futures, season_leaders_and_awards, the velocity archetype and the playoff-series archetype.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box scores and game logs (Stats API) for walk-offs, home runs and pitcher outs and runs; the sampled rules name only 'the Governing League'.
variants_and_edge_cases: Exposure differs by series: walk-offs and playoff home runs count all playoff games; KXMLBSERIESHR counts one series; KXMLBNEXTHR counts every MLB game in a date window (the sampled text does not restrict it to the regular season or one team); KXMLBSISTREAK runs until the streak breaks or the regular season ends.
KXMLBWALKOFFS is titled 'Walk-Off Home Runs' but its rule counts any walk-off ('The way the run scores does not matter'); the rule text governs (see unr_walkoff_title).

KXMLBSISTREAK counts partial innings at 1/3 per scoreless out but does not say whether an unearned run or an inherited runner who scores after the pitcher leaves breaks the streak (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; postseason innings are excluded, since the text runs the streak only until the regular season concludes, unr_streak_break_definition).

KXMLBSERIESHR has no start gate and no clause for a player who misses series games through injury or benching; KXMLBNEXTHR has no clause for injury, so a player on the injured list simply accrues no exposure and the market resolves No at the window end (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, unr_serieshr_missed_games).

all_star_week_events.label: All-Star Game and Home Run Derby events
contract_types: Home Run Derby winner, selections, Round 2 and finals qualifiers, Round 1 leader, final matchup and forecast
Home Run Derby Round 2 over/under, total HR, 500+ ft count, 525+ ft longest, longest HR and highest exit velocity
all_star_week_events.target: Result or player/event stat in the All-Star Game, the Futures Game or the Home Run Derby (winner, MVP, player hits/HR/strikeouts, total HR, Derby selection, advancement, round totals, longest HR, distance and exit-velocity extremes).
all_star_week_events.mechanism: All three events are exhibitions generated by who participates and how they are used, not by season-long roles. In the All-Star Game, selection and withdrawal define the pool, managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and a tie after nine innings goes to a swing-off whose statistics do not count for player props; the MVP is a panel and fan choice. The Futures Game is a seven-inning prospect exhibition priced from translated minor-league talent. In the 2026 Derby, an eight-player field takes 20 swings in a Round 1 pool and 15 in the semifinal and final, so homers are per-swing HR rate times a fixed allotment plus last-swing extensions, and longest-homer, 500+ ft and exit-velocity series are tail extremes over a draw count set by rounds reached.

inputs.why: Participation gate for every player market: appearance, slot and innings determine PA or batters faced.
Swing-off tiebreak regime (in force since 2022, first used 2025) decides the winner and which events count for player props versus the game total.
Field membership and seeding drive qualifier, matchup and finalist markets.
Fixed swing allotments per round, per-swing HR rate and last-swing extensions turn power into round totals and advancement.
Tail model for longest homer, 500 ft count and highest exit velocity.
League talent plus exhibition usage give the winner and MVP-conditioned structure.
Selection rules and vote phases determine who is on the roster pool for player markets.
Barrel, fly-ball and pull-air rate give per-swing and per-PA HR rates for ASG and Derby.
Bat speed and squared-up rate indicate raw power ceiling for derby tails and early-season hitters.
Host park HR factor and ball carry shift ASG HR counts and Derby distances.
Sector-level carry in the host park gives HR probability by batted-ball direction.
Wind along pull side changes HR odds in the ASG and distances in the Derby.
Temperature and altitude carry effect on distances, small but systematic for 500 ft tails.
Roof open or closed at host park removes or restores wind effect on the event.
Strikeout rate and whiff of the arms that pitch one inning each drive ASG strikeouts.
Starter versus reserve status maps to expected PA in a rotating-substitution exhibition.
Regular-season PA-by-slot numbers need replacing by exhibition PA counts; kept as a reference.
Handedness effect applies only mildly because pitchers rotate rather than match up deliberately.
Late scratches and withdrawals change participation and replacements before the event.
League-wide hitter strength of each roster informs winner market relative strength.
Shared game-day HR environment causes overdispersion in total ASG HR.
Past HR/FB luck regression gives per-swing HR probabilities for season-stat-based power.
Roster, pitcher and Derby announcements and refusals arrive via reports before official lists.
Rules fix non-appearance as No, swing-off exclusion for player props, and Yes-on-selection for the Derby selections market.
Each hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher shifts his per-swing HR rate under fixed swing counts.
Panel and fan selection of the MVP from winning-side key events and star profile settles the MVP series.
Translated minor-league talent of the two prospect rosters prices the Futures Game winner.

interactions.hypothesis: A hitter's expected ASG homers equal his chance of appearing times his expected PA times a small per-PA HR rate, so a power hitter on the bench contributes little while a starter contributes by a PA count that a regular-season lineup slot would overstate.

With swings fixed per round, a hittable and repeatable batting-practice pitcher raises HR per swing multiplicatively with the hitter's power, and the last-swing extension makes the gain convex for high-rate hitters.

Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.

Player HR props ignore swing-off homers, but the combined game-HR total is silent, so the total-HR distribution is a mixture over tie and no-tie regimes whose right tail depends on how the swing-off is counted.
MVP credit goes almost only to the winning side, so a player's MVP probability is his share of winning-side key events times the winner probability, with a star-name tilt in close calls.

interactions.how_to_test: Regress ASG HR on predicted P(any PA) x E[PA] x season HR rate versus season HR rate alone across 2012-2025 starters and reserves.

interactions.hypothesis: Under a fixed swing allotment the chosen pitcher's speed and location consistency scale the hitter's per-swing HR probability; the gain compounds through the last-swing extension, so a good pairing helps high-rate hitters more than low-rate ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit P(HR | swing) on Derby swing logs with hitter and pitcher random effects and their product; check whether pitcher effects are larger for hitters above the median HR rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.

interactions.hypothesis: Player HR props exclude swing-off homers by rule, but the combined game-HR rung does not say so; if swing-off homers count, a tied game adds a block of near-certain homers and gives the total a right tail, otherwise only nine innings matter.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the 7+ total under both counting rules using P(tie after nine) from 2012-2025 scores and compare the probability gap with the strike ladder.

interactions.hypothesis: Derby acceptance is correlated with All-Star selection, injury and hosting; a top slugger's refusal moves the replacement's expected power and the whole bracket jointly, not one participant at a time.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate field replacement sequences and test whether a joint acceptance model beats independent acceptance on historical Derby fields.

interactions.hypothesis: With the roof closed wind has no effect, with it open wind component along the pull side changes carry; the host park decides which regime is active.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact wind component with a roof-open indicator on historical Derby distances and ASG HR at retractable-roof hosts.

interactions.hypothesis: Rounds reached set how many homers a hitter contributes to the longest, 500+ ft and highest-EV draws, and the Round 1 tie rule rewards a long homer, so advancement and distance extremes are positively dependent and cannot be priced separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the event jointly versus with independent extreme draws and compare predicted longest-HR winner shares against 2015-2026 Derby outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: MVP probability is concentrated on the winning league, so a player's MVP chance is roughly winner probability times his share of winning-side key events; when the winner is a near coin flip, star-name bias in the fan ballot decides more close calls.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in per-swing HR rate: fixed-allotment mean plus a geometric last-swing extension p^2/(1-p)
nonlinearities.why: With n fixed swings the expected round total is about n*p plus an extension term that grows like p^2/(1-p), so high-rate hitters gain disproportionately and round totals have a right tail.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed (generalized Pareto) response above the hitter's 85th percentile
nonlinearities.why: Extreme markets resolve on the single largest distance or EV, so the mean has little information and the tail shape controls the probability.

nonlinearities.shape: step function: PA in {0,1,2,3} with a point mass at 0 that maps to No
nonlinearities.why: Rotating substitution makes PA small integers, and the rules settle non-appearance as No, so player-prop prices are zero-inflated and jump with starter versus reserve status.

mechanism_review.summary: All-Star Week outcomes come from three exhibition processes with no standings stakes. In the All-Star Game, a pool of selected players is cut by acceptance and withdrawal, the managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and a nine-inning tie goes to a swing-off whose statistics do not count for player props; a handful of plate appearances then produces hits, homers and strikeouts as rare-event counts, a non-appearance settles player props No, and the MVP is a panel-plus-fan judgement of winning-side events. The Futures Game is a seven-inning prospect game with its own talent scale. In the 2026 Derby, eight hitters take 20 swings in a Round 1 pool (top four advance) and 15 swings in the semifinal and final, so homers are a fixed allotment times per-swing HR rate (driven by power, selectivity and the chosen pitcher) plus last-swing extensions; distance and exit-velocity markets are extremes over homers whose number depends on rounds reached. Participation, not talent, is the dominant uncertainty for player markets.

stages.name: Selection, acceptance and withdrawal
stages.description: Rosters come from fan vote phases, player ballots and commissioner fill; Derby participants come from invitations that stars often decline. Between announcement and event, injuries and personal choices remove players and replacements enter. KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL settles on selection alone (Yes even if the player later withdraws), while every ASG player prop and every other Derby market resolves No for a non-participant, so this stage multiplies straight into those prices.
stages.distribution: Binary membership per player with correlated late changes; withdrawal hazard rises near the event date.

stages.name: Exhibition usage plan
stages.description: Two managers fill a card with starters, then rotate reserves; pitchers each throw about one inning in a planned order. This determines PA per hitter (zero to about three) and batters faced per arm, and so the chance that a named player enters at all, which the rules treat as No when he does not. Since 2022 (rule in place from the 2022 CBA, first used in 2025) a nine-inning tie is settled by a swing-off rather than extra innings, so regulation exposure is capped at nine innings.
stages.distribution: Discrete PA counts with many zeros and ones; pitcher batters faced concentrated at 3-5; regime shifts by year.

stages.name: Per-PA outcomes in the exhibition
stages.description: Given a PA, the hit, HR or strikeout chance depends on the hitter's contact and power profile and the arm's whiff and HR vulnerability, with hitters swinging freely and pitchers throwing at maximum effort for one inning. Host park and weather shift HR probability multiplicatively. Because PA counts are tiny, outcomes are rare-event Bernoulli draws with large relative variance.
stages.distribution: Low-count Bernoulli/Poisson-binomial; HR rate small per PA, so zero-inflated totals.

stages.name: Team score, winner and shared-day dispersion
stages.description: Runs and HR aggregate over both teams' exposures; a common day-level factor (wind, ball, pitcher usage) correlates HR counts across the game. The winner follows from nine-inning runs or, if tied, the swing-off. The combined game-HR rung (7+) is silent on swing-off homers, unlike the player props, so its tail depends on a counting rule the text does not give.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed team and HR totals; winner near coin-flip with league talent a mild tilt; MVP heavy-tailed credit.

stages.name: Derby rounds under the swing-capped format
stages.description: Round 1 is an eight-man pool of 20 swings each; the top four by homers advance, Round 1 ties broken by longest homer. Semifinal and final are head-to-head rounds of 15 swings, ties settled by three-swing swing-offs. A homer on the last allotted swing extends the round until a non-homer. Per-swing HR rate (power, selectivity, chosen pitcher, park) times the allotment sets round totals; Round 1 leader, Round 2 qualifier, Round 2 over/under, finalist, final matchup, forecast and winner markets all settle on this stage.
stages.distribution: Binomial count per round with a geometric last-swing extension tail; positive within-hitter correlation across rounds; advancement is an order statistic over the pool.

stages.name: Derby extremes: distance and exit velocity
stages.description: Longest homer, 500+ ft count, the 525 ft longest-distance threshold and highest exit velocity are order statistics over all Derby homers. They depend on each hitter's tail, on air carry at the host park and on how many homers he hits, which under fixed swings is set by rounds reached. They correlate with s5 through advancement and through the Round 1 longest-homer tiebreak, and ties are dead-heated at league-reported precision.
stages.distribution: Generalized Pareto/Gumbel-type tails; discrete 500+ counts; ties possible at reported precision.

stages.name: All-Star Game MVP selection
stages.description: After the game a panel with a fan ballot names the MVP. The choice concentrates on the winning league's player with the most visible contribution (go-ahead homer, multi-hit game, decisive swing-off moment), with a tilt toward star names in close calls. The MVP series therefore depends on winner probability, on each player's chance of producing a key event in his few plate appearances, and on voter bias.
stages.distribution: Categorical over roughly 60 players with heavy concentration on winning-side hitters with an HR or go-ahead hit; small residual mass on pitchers.

stages.name: Futures Game prospect exhibition
stages.description: The Futures Game is a seven-inning NL vs AL game of minor-league prospects played two days before the All-Star Game, with short pitcher stints and wide talent variation across levels. Strength comes from translated minor-league performance and prospect grades rather than major-league ratings; postponement within two days keeps the market open, otherwise it settles at a fair price.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli winner near 0.5 with a small talent tilt; high variance from seven innings and rotating arms.

opponent_matchup.note: Rotating one-inning arms (quality and handedness) in the game; the hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher in the Derby.

availability_news.note: Withdrawals, late replacements and participation announcements.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers of the prior pennant winners set lineup order and pitcher rotation by convention; encoded as substitution patterns.

environment.note: Host park, wind, density and roof affect HR counts and distances.

game_context_script.note: No stakes, rotating substitutions and a tiebreak rule shape the score path.

pace_volume.note: PA and batters faced in the game; fixed swing allotments plus extensions in the Derby.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-swing and per-PA HR and hit conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Tail of distance and EV, overdispersed total HR on a single day.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: The exhibition has no standings stakes; fatigue and the Sunday starter exclusion are folded into participation, so no separate schedule or motivation input is needed.

officiating_rules.note: Swing-off tiebreak regime in the game; swing caps, extension and tiebreak rules in the Derby; MVP selection procedure.

settlement_contract.note: Non-appearance is No, swing-off excluded for player props only, Yes-on-selection for Derby selections, dead heats; swing-off counting for totals is unresolved.

contract_review.settlement_definition: All 20 live series now have sampled rules text (2026 events). All-Star Game: KXMLBASGAME pays Yes if the National League wins the game 'originally scheduled for Jul 14, 2026'; a postponement within two days keeps the market open, longer or cancellation resolves at a fair price; a swing-off decides the winner. Named-player props KXMLBASGHIT (1+ hit), KXMLBASGHR (1+ HR) and KXMLBASGKS (2+ strikeouts) are per-player, resolve No if the player does not enter, and for hits/HR exclude swing-off statistics. KXMLBALLSTARHR counts home runs by all players combined (7+) with no swing-off clause. KXMLBASGMVP settles on the official MVP award. KXMLBFTGAME pays on the National League winning the Futures Game, with the same two-day postponement rule. Home Run Derby: winner, finals qualifier, Round 2 qualifier, Round 1 leader, longest HR and highest exit velocity resolve No if the player does not participate, with dead-heat 1/N on ties; the final matchup and forecast need both named players in the final; the Round 2 over/under counts the player's Round 2 homers (7+); KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL resolves Yes on selection even if the player then does not participate; event totals are HR count (140+), 500+ ft HR count (6+) and any HR of 525+ ft. Distance and exit velocity ties are judged 'according to the Governing League'.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Distance and exit-velocity ties are judged 'according to the Governing League' (MLB Statcast); other series name no source. Presumed: official MLB box scores for the All-Star and Futures Games, MLB MVP announcement, MLB Derby results.
variants_and_edge_cases: Player props KXMLBASGHIT/KXMLBASGHR exclude swing-off statistics; KXMLBALLSTARHR (combined game HR) has no such clause, so whether swing-off homers count toward the total is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Non-appearance is No (not void) for all ASG player props and for Derby participant markets, so participation probability multiplies the price; KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL is the exception and resolves Yes on selection.
KXMLBHRDERBYOU counts Round 2 homers only; a player eliminated in Round 1 has zero Round 2 homers and the text implies No, though it is not stated explicitly.
KXMLBHRDERBYR1LEAD and KXMLBHRDERBYSEMI dead-heat ties at 1/N, while the 2026 Derby itself breaks Round 1 ties by longest home run, so the market and the league can disagree on a tie.

2026 Derby format (press reports, June 2026): 20 swings in Round 1 pool play (top four advance), 15 swings in the semifinal and final, a homer on the last swing extends the round, semifinal/final ties go to a three-swing swing-off; whether swing-off and extension homers count toward event totals, 500+ ft counts and longest HR is not stated.
KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBFTGAME survive a postponement of up to two days; beyond that they resolve to a fair price, not void.
KXMLBASGMVP settles on the official award, which is chosen by a panel with a fan ballot component whose weight is not stated in the rules.

labour_stoppage_and_season_schedule.label: Labour stoppage and league season-schedule markets
contract_types: Regular-season games played above a threshold
labour_stoppage_and_season_schedule.target: Whether the MLB regular season starts before a date or plays more than N games, as determined by collective bargaining, any lockout or strike, and the games the league cancels.
labour_stoppage_and_season_schedule.mechanism: The outcome is produced by owner-union collective bargaining after the CBA expires on December 1, 2026, not by games. Agreement before or after expiry, an owners' lockout decision, deadline hazards (spring training, scheduled opener) and the ramp-up after a deal set the first game date. More than 600 of 2,430 games fails only if no season is staged or play starts around mid-August, so that contract turns on a late go/no-go decision about a truncated season (2020 versus 1994-95) and on the non-agreement route of impasse, replacement players or an NLRB injunction.

inputs.why: Gap between owner and union stated positions governs the chance a deal is reached before games are lost.
Calendar of expiry, report and scheduled opening dates turns bargaining state into dated hazards.
Few comparable stoppages exist, so a reference class gives the prior for stoppage length.
Estimated revenue and pay at risk for each side determine who concedes; revenue splits are third-party estimates.
Maps start date to games playable; locates the late-start cutoff for 600 games, where compression no longer matters.
CBA expiry date, lockout flag, expected end and transaction freeze rules define the regime.
Scenario table of lockout probability, start and end dates, and games lost under each case.
Reports of talks, offers and deadlines arrive before official statements.
Source reliability weights leaks about proposals and sessions when sources conflict.
Official-game and suspended-game rules decide how partially played games count toward games played.
Service-time and roster-freeze rules show what changes during a lockout; indirect effect on bargaining topics.
Transaction timeline shows whether a freeze is on; informative about lockout state only.
Payroll and tax position indicates owner demands on cost control.
Free-agent class and arbitration status signal how many players feel urgent pressure.
Exact wording of the first-game and games-played conditions fixes what counts.
Market lifecycle events (halts, rule edits) identify when contract text changes.
Whether a minimum truncated season is staged or the year is cancelled decides the 600-game contract.
Impasse, replacement players and an NLRB injunction are a non-agreement route to games being played.

interactions.hypothesis: The hazard of agreement in a given week is a baseline deadline hazard scaled by the gap size; the same deadline closes a small gap with high probability and a structural gap (such as a cap demand) with low probability, so the effect of a deadline depends on how wide the gap is.

Once the remaining calendar falls below a minimum viable season, staging depends on whether postseason media revenue is at risk for owners and pay is pro-rated for players; the same calendar date gives opposite outcomes under different leverage.

The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.

Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.

interactions.how_to_test: Fit weekly hazard with gap index, deadline proximity and their product on stoppage episodes and test the product term, using the 2021-22 and 1990 cases as holdouts.

interactions.hypothesis: When the remaining calendar drops below a minimum viable season, the outcome flips from 'play a short season' to 'cancel' depending on whether owners' postseason media revenue is at risk and players get pro-rated pay; above the threshold leverage matters little for the 600 strike.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast 2020 (staged with media money at stake) and 1994-95 (cancelled) and score the model on reported proposals by date; check that P(staged) is flat until the calendar threshold.

interactions.hypothesis: The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition historical durations on a revenue-guarantee indicator across MLB, NHL and NBA episodes and compare tails.

interactions.hypothesis: Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate hazards by regime flag and test whether news-dated shifts in agreement odds differ before and after the lockout start.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening Day before May 31 needs agreement or an injunction at least a ramp-up period earlier; filing of an NLRB complaint adds a second hazard path whose timing is set by the court, not by deadlines, so the deal-date step can be bypassed.
interactions.how_to_test: Reconstruct 1995 (injunction March 31, games late April) and 2021-22 timelines and test whether a two-path hazard fits first-game dates better than a bargaining-only hazard.

nonlinearities.shape: spiking hazard near hard deadlines (expiry, report date, scheduled opener) and flat between
nonlinearities.why: Concessions concentrate when costs become real, so the probability of agreement is not smooth in time and a constant-hazard model misestimates both short and long stoppages.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in days remaining: P(season staged) high until remaining calendar falls below a minimum viable season, then drops sharply
nonlinearities.why: Owners and players accept a short season only while it still carries a postseason and enough games to justify pro-rated pay, so the 600-game outcome is a step in the date of any deal.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: little effect until a red-line item is declared, then a large drop in near-term agreement probability
nonlinearities.why: Structural disputes such as a salary cap do not close with small concessions, so the gap index matters mainly once it crosses a structural level.

mechanism_review.summary: Neither contract is decided on the field. The outcome is a bargaining process between ownership and the players' union after the collective agreement expires on December 1, 2026: whether a deal precedes expiry, whether owners lock out, how long agreement takes at the deadlines (spring-training reporting, scheduled opener), and the ramp-up needed before games. Opening Day before May 31 requires agreement, or an injunction or imposed terms, plus a ramp-up before that date. More than 600 of 2,430 games fails only if no season is staged or play starts around mid-August, so that contract is a deep-tail question decided by a late go/no-go on a truncated season (2020 staged 60 games; 1994-95 cancelled) and by the impasse, replacement-player and labour-board route, not by make-up scheduling.

stages.name: Bargaining state before and after CBA expiry
stages.description: The agreement expires on December 1, 2026. Before then the owners decide whether to bargain to a deal, accept an extension or prepare a lockout; the union decides whether to authorize a strike. Positions on economic structure (cap, floor, revenue sharing, tax, pre-arbitration pay) set whether a gap exists and its size. The state is dynamic, updated by each session and each public proposal.
stages.distribution: Discrete state (deal, no deal and talks, lockout) with long persistence; gap index changes in jumps at meetings and leaks.

stages.name: Stoppage duration hazard
stages.description: If no deal exists at expiry, the owners may lock out and stay out until costs rise. Hazard of agreement rises at deadlines: spring-training reporting, the scheduled opener, first missed paychecks. Reference classes (1990, 2021-22 and 1994-95 in baseball; NHL and NBA lockouts) show durations from days to a full season. The question is the cumulative probability that agreement lands before the date that permits play by May 31.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed duration with spikes at deadlines; right-censored; very small sample of comparable events.

stages.name: Ramp-up and first-game date
stages.description: After an agreement, players need a ramp-up period (spring training of about 3-4 weeks) and the league needs to publish a revised schedule. The first regular-season game therefore occurs at a lag after the deal that depends on the date and on whether the league shortens the preparation. Opening Day before May 31 requires the deal and ramp-up to fit before that date.
stages.distribution: Deterministic lag with small variance conditional on deal date; discontinuity at late dates where the league may cancel the season instead.

stages.name: Truncated-season go/no-go and games played
stages.description: If no deal exists late in the calendar, the parties decide whether to stage a minimum season for postseason and media revenue or cancel. The 600-game strike is about 40-46 days of league play, so doubleheaders and make-up dates are irrelevant to it; what matters is whether any season of at least about 40 games per team is staged. Mid-season stoppages matter only if they begin before roughly 600 games are complete.
stages.distribution: Trimodal: mass near the full 2,430 when a deal lands by spring, a smaller mode at 600-900 for a late truncated season, and a point mass at zero for cancellation.

stages.name: Settlement resolution and official count
stages.description: Opening Day resolves on whether the first 2027 regular-season game has taken place before May 31 and the games-played contract resolves on the count of MLB regular-season games above 600. Postponements, suspended games and tiebreakers are matters of official counting. Both depend on the contract text being read precisely.
stages.distribution: Binary on date; integer count near the schedule total; edge cases are rare.

stages.name: Non-agreement route: impasse, replacement players and injunction
stages.description: Owners may declare impasse and implement terms or schedule replacement-player games, and the union may file unfair-labour-practice charges; an NLRB complaint and federal injunction can restore prior terms and return players without a new agreement, as in March-April 1995. This route can start the season earlier than bargaining alone would, and it raises a counting question for both contracts if replacement-player games are played.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete states with long gaps between filings; a granted injunction gives a short fixed lag to play.

talent_strength.note: Team and player quality do not determine whether owners and the union reach a deal; the outcome is a league-wide bargaining process, not a contest between rosters.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or matchup in a collective bargaining process; the closest analogue is the gap between the two sides' positions, covered under motivation and timeline inputs.

role_personnel.note: Who negotiates: commissioner, owners' committee, union leadership and membership votes.

availability_news.note: Reports of sessions, offers and lockout decisions with source reliability.

coaching_scheme.note: The bargaining strategy of each side (hardline versus incremental, public versus private) plays the role of tactics.

environment.note: Economic environment: revenue, television contracts and finance conditions that set each side's cost of waiting.

game_context_script.note: Expected path of the negotiation over the calendar, from expiry to the scheduled opener.

pace_volume.note: Games playable after a given start date; irrelevant at the 600 strike except to locate the late-start cutoff.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate exists; the outcome is a duration and a schedule count, so the nearest analogue is the hazard of agreement per week under the timeline input.

distribution_variance.note: Heavy-tailed duration and a trimodal games-played distribution (full, truncated, cancelled).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Deadlines, paychecks and stakes drive concessions.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league rules on lockout, freeze and schedule revision; labour-law route of impasse, replacement players and injunction.

settlement_contract.note: Wording of before-date and above-threshold conditions; some edge cases unresolved.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXMLBOPENINGDAY settles Yes if the first game of the 2027 MLB regular season has taken place before May 31, 2027. KXMLBSEASONGAMES settles Yes if the number of MLB regular-season games played in 2027 is above 600 (strike type greater, floor 600), read as league games of 2,430 scheduled, though team-games are not excluded by the text. The rules do not define whether suspended or shortened games count, whether games staged with replacement players count as 'MLB regular season games', the time zone of the date boundary, or a data source, so verification is partial.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules. Presumed: official MLB schedule results and the league's game log (MLB Stats API).
variants_and_edge_cases: The opener series settles on when the first game occurred, not when it was scheduled; if a lockout moves the opening to May 30 versus May 31 the date boundary matters and time zone is not stated.
Strike type greater means exactly 600 games resolves No; one rung is sampled and other thresholds may exist for the same series.

Count unit: 'number of MLB regular season games played' is most naturally league games (2,430 scheduled), but team-games (4,860) are not excluded; 600 is about 40 games per team on the league-game reading.
Suspended or shortened games are not addressed. Tiebreaker games (Game 163) were abolished from 2022 and matter only if a new CBA reinstates them.
An international opening series (MLB opened 2025 in Tokyo in mid-March) would be the 'first game' for KXMLBOPENINGDAY; relevant only if a deal lands close to the scheduled opener.
Games staged with replacement players after an owners' impasse declaration (1995 spring precedent) would plausibly be 'MLB regular season games' for both contracts; the text does not say.

A season that begins on time but later suffers a mid-season strike would affect the games-played contract but not the Opening Day contract; once 601 games are played the games contract is settled Yes.

playoff_series_markets.label: Playoff series winner, total games, spread and games hosted
playoff_series_markets.target: Winner, number of games, game margin of a best-of-N postseason series, or number of playoff games a club hosts.
playoff_series_markets.mechanism: A series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that differ by game: the bracket sets the home pattern, off days and rainouts move the rotation so each game has a different starter, bullpen fatigue accumulates (worse after extra innings, which have no automatic runner in the postseason) and resets, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games, spread and exact score are functions of the same series score; games hosted is seed probability times rounds reached times the home pattern, so before the bracket is set it is driven by regular-season seeding.

inputs.why: Home-game allocation by round, seed and length, with designated home team logged per game.
Market-free per-game win probability from starters, bullpen state, lineup and home edge; every series contract is a function of it.
Starter assignment per game under off-day compression determines per-game win probability.
Accumulated reliever fatigue changes late-series strength and the length of the series.
Round-specific rosters and injury returns change strength between series.
Series state, games played, off days and home-field pattern drive the remaining path.
Elimination and leverage state of the series inform manager decisions in the next game.
Marginal of the exact-score output; kept only to map total-games strikes, not as a predictor.
Output layer that maps the per-game win vector to winner, margin, length and exact-score cells.
Model machinery that enumerates bracket paths from seed probabilities for hosting and later opponents.
Rating based on top starters, top relievers and the regular lineup suits short series.
Short leash and high-leverage reliever usage compress talent gaps in the playoffs.
Starter true talent feeds the per-game win probability with the assignment table.
Bullpen quality matters more in playoff games as relievers pitch a larger share of innings.
Lineup offence against the handedness of the starters expected in the series.
Injuries before and during the series with point-in-time vintages.
Seeding, byes and tiebreaks define who hosts which game.
Tiebreak state decides byes and Wild Card hosting among close teams before seeds are final.
Rotation slot and rest days for each starter before and during the series.
Park-specific home advantage is small but enters the per-game probability and hosting.
Talent prior from projections; weak late in the season but used as shrinkage target.
Seed probabilities from the remaining regular season drive hosting markets priced before the bracket is set.
Plate umpire zone tendencies shift single-game scoring a little.
Series winner, total games and spread wording determines what counts as a game or a margin.
Residual within-series correlation widens the score distribution and moves sweep and seven-game cells.

interactions.hypothesis: An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.

A favourite's per-game edge raises sweep probability convexly, and positive residual dependence fattens both the 4-0 and 4-3 cells, so spread and exact-score markets react to dependence much more than winner markets do.
Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.

The probability of hosting 8 or more games is near zero for seeds 5-6 and depends on reaching the pennant round for bye seeds, so seed probability gates the hosting strike as a step rather than a smooth effect.

An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game bullpen availability on prior starter innings and rest, then compare win probability residuals in postseason games after bullpen days.

interactions.hypothesis: Residual dependence between games widens the score distribution for a given per-game edge: sweeps and seventh games both become more likely while the winner probability barely moves, so spread and exact-score cells respond to dependence and winner markets do not.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed 4-0 and 4-3 frequencies (1995-2025) against simulations from fitted per-game vectors with rho = 0 versus the estimated rho, stratified by per-game edge.

interactions.hypothesis: Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rating variants (full roster versus top-heavy weighting) in predicting playoff game outcomes across 2012-2025.

interactions.hypothesis: Seed fixes which hosting totals are reachable: 8+ needs at least the pennant round for a bye seed, is easier for seed 3-4 through three Wild Card home games, and is nearly impossible for seed 5-6, so seed probability enters the hosting strike as a gate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(hosts >= k) conditional on final seed and rounds reached across 2022-2025 brackets and compare with a model that uses series win probability without seed.

interactions.hypothesis: Under elimination the trailing manager shortens starters' leash and uses top relievers early, so win probability behaves differently in elimination games than in game one of a series.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact elimination flag with starter innings share and test whether game win probability residuals differ for elimination versus non-elimination games.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the per-game edge: sweep probability rises faster than linearly as the favourite strengthens
nonlinearities.why: Series outcome is a binomial-type path function, so a small per-game edge becomes a larger series edge and sweep-only spread and exact-score cells change nonlinearly.

nonlinearities.shape: step changes in win probability by starter identity, with a tail for bullpen games
nonlinearities.why: The best starter pitches a game with a clearly higher win probability, and a bullpen game lowers it, so per-game strength is multimodal across games.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in rounds reached; integer-valued sum with a jump at each round
nonlinearities.why: Home games are added in blocks by round, so the count is a lumpy function of advancement rather than a smooth variable.

mechanism_review.summary: A playoff series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that are not identical: the bracket fixes who hosts which game, each game has a different announced starter after off-day compression or a rainout, relievers accumulate fatigue (amplified by postseason extra innings without an automatic runner) and reset on off days, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games, game spread and exact score are functions of one final score (a margin above 3.5 games in a best-of-seven needs a 4-0 sweep), so the information inputs are the per-game probability vector and the dependence between games; the score distribution is output, not input. Playoff games hosted is the sum of designated home games over rounds reached; before the bracket exists it is driven by regular-season seed probabilities.

stages.name: Bracket, seeding and series format
stages.description: The 12-team bracket sets who plays whom: seeds 1-2 get byes, seeds 3-6 play a best-of-3 Wild Card Series hosted entirely by seeds 3-4, then best-of-5 and best-of-7 rounds with fixed home patterns. For hosting contracts priced before the season ends, seed probabilities from the remaining schedule and tiebreak rules are the dominant input; for single-series contracts this stage only fixes best-of-N and home pattern.
stages.distribution: Discrete bracket paths; deterministic format given seeds; path probabilities driven by upstream series results.

stages.name: Rosters, injuries and round-specific strength
stages.description: Each series has a submitted roster; injured players may return or be replaced between rounds, and key injuries during a series change strength. Team quality is therefore round-specific and uses a playoff-weighted rating (top starters, top relievers, regular lineup) rather than the full season average.
stages.distribution: Discrete roster states with continuous strength shifts; injury arrival roughly Poisson with heavy impact for stars.

stages.name: Starter assignment and rest under off days
stages.description: Postseason schedules have off days, so managers use three or four starters and may use an ace on short rest or a bullpen game. The identity of the starter in each game defines that game's win probability and the series is a sequence of different matchups rather than repeated draws of the same one. Rainouts and postponements move the off days, which changes rest and therefore which starter pitches each later game.
stages.distribution: Categorical starter per game with conditional dependence on prior games; bullpen-game tail.

stages.name: Per-game win probability and bullpen fatigue
stages.description: Given starters, lineups and park, a game is a win-probability draw with a small home edge. Short leashes make the bullpen cover a larger share of innings, and fatigue accumulates across consecutive games, resetting on off days. This couples games within a series: a heavy bullpen game two days ago lowers the next game's strength. Postseason extra innings use no automatic runner, so a long game can strip several relievers for the next one or two games.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with probability varying by game and weakly correlated across games through shared fatigue.

stages.name: Series dynamic program: winner, length, margin, exact score
stages.description: The series result is the first-to-N-wins path through the per-game probability vector, widened by any residual dependence between games. Winner, total games, margin (spread) and exact score are functions of one path; a sweep gives the largest margin and the shortest length. The state at the snapshot (games played, score, elimination) fixes the remaining tree. The score distribution is computed here as output; it is not an input.
stages.distribution: Discrete path distribution over scores 4-0 to 4-3 (or 3-0 to 3-2); lengths 4-7; correlated margins and lengths.

stages.name: Hosting count convolution and settlement
stages.description: For hosted-games contracts the count is the sum over rounds reached of designated home games in each series played, from the allocation table, seed and series length. Seeds 1-2 host 2-11 (DS games 1-2 are always theirs), seeds 3-4 host 2-13 because they host the whole Wild Card Series, seeds 5-6 host 0-10. Settlement uses official game counts; 'hosts' at a relocated or temporary park is undefined in the rules.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent integer sum; support 2-11 for bye seeds, 2-13 for seeds 3-4, 0-10 for seeds 5-6; lumpy, jumps by round.

opponent_matchup.note: Offence versus expected starters and handedness of the specific series.

role_personnel.note: Starters per game and round-specific rosters.

availability_news.note: Injuries and reliever availability inside the series.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager rotation use, leash and leverage deployment.

environment.note: Venue and umpire effects; weather enters through postponements that move rest days (handled in starter assignment), not as a run-level input.

pace_volume.note: Games remaining in the series state and home games allocated per round reached.

efficiency_conversion.note: The contracts are decided by game wins, not by a conversion rate of a repeated opportunity; per-game win probability is a composite handled in team rating and starter inputs, with no independent efficiency variable.

distribution_variance.note: Residual within-series dependence sets the width of the score distribution (sweep and seven-game cells).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding, byes, tiebreaks and remaining-season seed probabilities.

officiating_rules.note: Postseason format, series length and extra-inning rules; umpiring is secondary.

settlement_contract.note: Winner, over/under, at-least, spread, exact-score and hosted-games wording; unfinished series and the meaning of 'hosts' are unresolved.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with sampled rules text, all quoting World Series-style 'Championship Series' pairings (TB vs MIL 2026, TOR vs LAD 2025). KXMLBSERIES pays Yes if the named club wins the named series. KXMLBSERIESGAMES pays Yes if more than the strike (6.5) games are played; KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL pays Yes if the series has at least the strike (7) games, the same event expressed as greater_or_equal. KXMLBSERIESSPREAD pays Yes if the club wins by more than the strike in games (3.5, i.e. a 4-0 sweep in a best-of-seven). KXMLBSERIESEXACT and KXMLBSERIESSCORE pay Yes on one exact series record (e.g. 4-3 for the named club); they are the same contract under two tickers. KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST pays Yes if the club hosts at least the strike (8) playoff games over the whole postseason. No sampled text covers suspended or unfinished series, a relocated or neutral-site home game, or names a data source.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled rules text. Presumed: official MLB postseason results and box scores (MLB Stats API), including the designated home team per game.
variants_and_edge_cases: Spread above 3.5 is only reachable in a best-of-seven (4-0); in a best-of-five the maximum margin is 3, so the same-form market would settle No structurally.

Total games: KXMLBSERIESGAMES (over 6.5, strike_type greater) and KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL (at least 7, greater_or_equal) are the same event in a best-of-seven; other rungs or shorter rounds need format-specific strikes.
Exact score: KXMLBSERIESEXACT and KXMLBSERIESSCORE each pay on one of eight cells (4-0..4-3 for either club); the cells sum to one, so the ladder is a full partition.

Hosting support by seed under the 12-team format: seeds 1-2 host 2-11 (DS games 1-2 are always at home; max DS 3 + LCS 4 + WS 4); seeds 3-4 host 2-13 (all of a best-of-3 Wild Card Series, then at most 2 in a DS as lower seed); seeds 5-6 host 0 in the Wild Card Series.

'Hosts' is not defined: a designated home game played at a temporary park (Athletics in Sacramento 2025-27), a borrowed park, or a neutral site after relocation could settle either way (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).
Suspended games, rainouts or a series that does not finish are not addressed in any sampled rules text (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

Kalshi labels the World Series 'Championship Series' (ticker suffix WS, cross-league pairing); sampled markets are all World Series, so League Championship or Division Series variants are inferred, not seen.

amateur_draft_selection.label: MLB Draft pick position markets
amateur_draft_selection.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall pick or within the top N picks of the MLB Draft.
amateur_draft_selection.mechanism: The MLB Draft is a sequential without-replacement selection. The order of clubs at slots 1-10 is fixed by the lottery (picks 1-6), reverse prior-season record, luxury-tax pick moves and inserted compensation picks, and first-round picks cannot be traded. Each club then takes the highest player on its own board after adjusting for its bonus pool strategy, its front-office tendency and each prospect's medicals and signability; many top picks are pre-agreed below slot. A prospect's slot is therefore the outcome of consensus talent rank, club-specific deviation and the cascade of choices ahead of him.

inputs.why: Club identity at each overall slot conditions every exact-slot probability.
Lottery draws set picks 1-6 before the order is known; needed for markets priced before the lottery.
Mean and spread of public board ranks locate the prospect's likely selection window.
Final mocks and pre-draft bonus agreement reports link the prospect to a club and slot.
Weights each insider's club-player link by that source's historical accuracy.
Shows which kinds of clubs value the prospect above or below consensus.
Medical flags and bonus demands drive draft-day slides below talent rank.
Club-specific preference decides whether the club at a slot takes the consensus player.
Pool budget and underslot incentives explain picks that depart from talent order.
Structural requirement, not an information source: the without-replacement engine that keeps exact-slot and top-10 probabilities consistent across prospects.
Clubs far over the top tax threshold have their first pick moved back ten slots.
A lockout after the CBA expiry could postpone or reshape the next draft.
Defines exact-slot versus top-N construction and which draft year counts.

interactions.hypothesis: A prospect's exact-slot chance depends on whether the club at that slot historically prefers his profile, so the same board rank gives different slot odds under different orders.
Insider links carry most information when boards disagree; when boards agree tightly, reports add little beyond the consensus rank.
Clubs pursuing underslot deals favour low-leverage college seniors, so high-demand prep players slide further at slots held by pool-constrained clubs.
A medical or bonus-demand flag moves a top-three prospect little but pushes a prospect ranked 6-12 out of the top 10, so the slide depends on consensus rank.

The probability that a prospect goes at slot k is conditional on which club holds k: a club that takes college bats almost exclusively raises a college hitter's slot-k chance and lowers a prep pitcher's, independently of board rank.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2012-2025 first rounds, regress (pick minus consensus rank) on prospect class interacted with the picking club's prior college share; a significant interaction confirms conditionality.

interactions.hypothesis: When boards agree (rank SD below about 2) the consensus rank predicts the slot well and insider links add little; when boards disagree, the selection is decided by club-specific links and reports dominate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare exact-slot log loss of consensus-only versus consensus-plus-final-mock models, split by cross-board rank SD tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: A high bonus demand only causes a slide at slots held by clubs planning underslot deals; at slots held by clubs paying full slot it costs little, so slide risk is demand times the club's underslot propensity.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress slide (pick minus rank) on reported demand flag x picking-club underslot score among top-30 ranked prep players.

interactions.hypothesis: A medical or demand flag moves a prospect differently by rank: a top-three player with a flag still goes inside the top 10, while a player ranked 6-12 with the same flag slides out of it, because no club at the top needs to take the risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress slide (pick minus consensus rank) on flag indicator interacted with consensus rank tercile among top-30 prospects in 2012-2025 drafts.

interactions.hypothesis: A club-player link moves probability in proportion to the reporting writer's historical exact-slot hit rate; a link from a low-accuracy mock is close to noise.
interactions.how_to_test: Score writers' final mocks 2015-2025 by exact-slot hits and test whether reliability-weighted link shares beat equal-weight shares.

nonlinearities.shape: convex spread of selection window in mean rank
nonlinearities.why: Slot variance grows faster than linearly with mean rank: top-two prospects almost never fall more than two slots, while prospects ranked 8-15 can land anywhere from 4 to 30, so exact-slot probability decays steeply with rank.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: discrete slide when a flag is reported
nonlinearities.why: Medical or demand flags do not shift slot smoothly; a credible report removes the player from several clubs' boards at once, producing a jump of many slots rather than a proportional move.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in record rank via lottery cutoffs
nonlinearities.why: Lottery odds are flat among the worst three clubs and fall in steps; outside the lottery, order is deterministic, so a one-win difference in prior record can move a club across a step.

mechanism_review.summary: Where a prospect is drafted is decided by a sequence of club choices, not by one event. First the slot-to-club map is fixed: a lottery among non-playoff clubs sets picks 1-6, the rest of the non-playoff clubs follow in reverse record, luxury-tax penalties move some clubs back, compensation picks are inserted, and first-round picks cannot be traded, so the map is known before the draft. Each club then values prospects from its own board, built from tools, performance and tracking data, and adjusts for medicals, bonus demands and its bonus-pool plan; many top picks are agreed below slot in advance and leaked by insiders. The named player's slot is where the first club that most prefers him among those still available chooses him. Exact-slot contracts are sharp point masses within this cascade; top-10 contracts are the cumulative sum.

stages.name: Slot-to-club map
stages.description: The lottery draws picks 1-6 among the 18 non-playoff clubs with odds weighted toward the worst records and eligibility restrictions on repeat winners; remaining non-playoff clubs fill the following slots in reverse record; a club $40M or more over the base luxury-tax threshold has its highest pick moved back ten slots; prior-year failed-to-sign compensation picks are inserted. No first-round trades are allowed, so after the order is published this stage is deterministic.
stages.distribution: Discrete lottery permutation before the draw (multinomial over six slots), degenerate after the official order is published.

stages.name: Prospect valuation and consensus
stages.description: Clubs and public evaluators rank the class from tool grades, opponent-adjusted college or showcase performance, tracked exit velocity, swing decisions or pitch quality, and age relative to class. Public boards are correlated with club boards; the mean rank sets the centre of the selection window and cross-board disagreement sets its width. Rankings move with spring performance, injuries and showcase results, so the board vintage matters.
stages.distribution: Rank variable with heteroscedastic spread: tight for the top two or three prospects, widening sharply beyond about the fifth.

stages.name: Club-specific deviation: tendency, pool and signability
stages.description: Each club deviates from consensus according to its front-office preferences (college bats, prep arms), its bonus-pool plan (underslot at the top to fund later overslot picks), and each prospect's medical flags and bonus demand backed by college commitment. These deviations are persistent within a scouting-director regime and are the main reason exact slots differ from board order.
stages.distribution: Club-level random effects plus a left-skewed slide tail for flagged or high-demand players; occasional large reaches by underslot clubs.

stages.name: Pre-draft agreements and insider information
stages.description: In the final days clubs narrow to a few players and often agree bonuses with advisors before the pick; national writers publish final mocks and club-player links. These reports are the most informative signal for exact slots near the top, but writers differ in accuracy and late changes happen on draft night, so each link must be timestamped and weighted by source track record.
stages.distribution: Information arrives in jumps; slot probabilities concentrate quickly in the final 24-48 hours, with residual surprise from draft-night changes.

stages.name: Sequential selection cascade and settlement
stages.description: Picks are made in order without replacement: the named player is taken at slot k only if no earlier club took him and the club at k prefers him to everyone remaining. Upsets ahead shift him down; reaches ahead shift him up. The exact-slot contract settles on a single overall number and the top-10 contract on the cumulative event; the draft itself could be disrupted by a labour stoppage only for 2027-draft series (CBA expires 1 December 2026).
stages.distribution: Joint without-replacement distribution over prospects and slots; exact slot is a sharp, multi-modal point mass; cumulative top-N is monotone in N.

talent_strength.note: Talent is the prospect's projected value as judged by boards and his performance profile.

opponent_matchup.note: No contest takes place: the draft is a selection among clubs, and competition between clubs for a player is handled by the sequential selection model, not an opponent matchup.

role_personnel.note: Which club sits at each slot and the prospect's position and class profile.

availability_news.note: Medical reports, bonus demands and insider club links with source weighting.

coaching_scheme.note: Front-office and scouting-director drafting philosophy plays the role of scheme.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel do not affect club selections on draft night; park and conference context of prospect stats is adjusted inside the performance profile.

game_context_script.note: The in-draft state (who has been taken before each slot) is the analogue of game script and drives cascades. Structural requirement (derived model), not an information source; the only live in-draft state is the list of picks already made.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities: each slot is one selection, and the number of picks before the threshold is fixed by the contract (5th, top 10).

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity success rate exists; the outcome is an ordinal selection, not a conversion of attempts, so efficiency has no meaning here.

distribution_variance.note: Joint without-replacement slot distribution with cascade dependence. Structural requirement (derived model), not an information source; the only live in-draft state is the list of picks already made.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Pool incentives for underslot picks and labour calendar risk to the draft.

officiating_rules.note: Lottery, order, tax-penalty and compensation-pick rules.

settlement_contract.note: Exact overall slot versus top-N cumulative wording; source and compensation-pick numbering unresolved.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXMLBDRAFTPICK settles YES only if the named prospect is selected at the stated overall slot (sample: 5th overall) in the stated draft year; KXMLBDRAFTTOP settles YES if he is selected at any slot within the top N (sample: top 10) of that draft. Selection, not signing, is what the text names, so an unsigned pick still appears to count. The text names no source of truth, does not say whether inserted compensation picks are numbered as overall picks, and says nothing about a postponed or cancelled draft.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules text; presumably the official MLB draft results (MLB.com draft tracker / MLB Stats API draft endpoint).
variants_and_edge_cases: Exact-slot (KXMLBDRAFTPICK) versus cumulative top-N (KXMLBDRAFTTOP): for one prospect the exact-slot probabilities over 1..10 must sum to the top-10 probability.

Inserted round-1 compensation picks for prior-year unsigned first-rounders can change which club holds a given overall number; Prospect Promotion Incentive picks are understood to be placed after round 1 and so not to renumber slots 1-10 (CBA text unverified); whether Kalshi counts inserted picks as overall picks is unstated.
A prospect who is drafted but does not sign appears to satisfy 'selected'/'drafted'; signing is not mentioned.
No clause covers a postponed, shortened or cancelled draft (as in 2020) or a prospect withdrawing or being ruled ineligible before the draft.
rules_secondary is empty for both sampled markets, so no resolution source is named.

pitch_velocity_extremes.label: Season maximum pitch velocity thresholds (player or league-wide)
pitch_velocity_extremes.target: Whether a named pitcher, or any pitcher, throws a pitch at or above a velocity threshold (e.g. 107 MPH) in any game of the season including playoffs, per tracked pitch speed.
pitch_velocity_extremes.mechanism: The season's fastest pitch is the maximum of a bounded per-pitch speed distribution taken over a few thousand near-peak fastballs from a small pool of elite throwers. Exceeding a threshold beyond the tracked record needs a pitcher whose ceiling sits close to it, enough max-effort attempts (relief use, postseason), favourable situations (rest, warmth, leverage), continued health and a tracking reading that lands above the line. The tail is bounded by physiology, so exceedance probabilities beyond the observed record fall off faster than an exponential tail would imply.

inputs.why: Identifies which arms have tracked peaks close enough to the threshold to matter.
Bounded-tail extreme-value engine that turns peaks and exposure into exceedance probability.
Remaining number of near-peak fastballs, including postseason weighted by qualification odds.
Starter pacing versus max-effort relief changes how close each pitch is to the ceiling.
Leverage, postseason, rest and temperature shift the upper tail for a given pitch.
Elite throwers lose exposure to arm injury, eroding the candidate pool.
Recent velocity trajectory shows whether a candidate is near or below his peak form.
Current IL status with point-in-time vintage zeroes near-term exposure.
Park offsets, data revisions and rounding decide borderline readings.
Game-time temperature feeds the situational lift on velocity.
Short postseason leashes and high-leverage bullpen use raise near-peak attempts.
Workload caps on young hard throwers truncate appearances and near-peak exposure.
Threshold, inclusion of playoffs and named-versus-any construction.
Frequency of glitch or mis-tagged readings in the raw live feed and how fast they are corrected; a non-physical route to a 107 reading.

interactions.hypothesis: Exceedance requires both a near-threshold ceiling and many attempts; volume without ceiling contributes almost nothing, so the two multiply inside the tail.
Postseason bullpen use of hard-throwing starters converts paced pitches into max-effort pitches, concentrating record chances in October.
The situational lift (temperature included as a fixed effect) shifts the per-pitch mean, and at a threshold beyond the record a small additive lift multiplies the tail probability.
A falling velocity trend signals elevated injury hazard, so exposure loss and lower ceiling arrive together rather than independently.

Season exceedance is roughly 1 - exp(-N x p): N near-peak pitches times the per-pitch tail p given the ceiling. A pitcher topping out 3 mph below the line has p near zero, so even thousands of pitches add nothing; exposure only matters for arms whose ceiling is close.
interactions.how_to_test: Across 2015-2025, regress whether a pitcher's season max exceeded his prior-season 99.9th percentile by 1 mph on log near-peak pitch count interacted with distance from that percentile.

interactions.hypothesis: A starter moved to the October bullpen switches from paced effort to max effort, raising his top-speed distribution by one to three mph for the remaining appearances; regular-season starter exposure says little about this regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare within-pitcher 99th-percentile fastball speed in postseason relief versus regular-season starts for starters used in relief in 2015-2025 postseasons.

interactions.hypothesis: An additive lift (leverage, rest, temperature, all fixed effects inside the lift input) shifts the per-pitch distribution, and because the threshold sits in the bounded tail, tail probability rises convexly with the lift until close to the endpoint.
interactions.how_to_test: Count pitches above each pitcher's personal 99.9th percentile by temperature and leverage bins; check that the ratio grows faster than the mean speed shift.

interactions.hypothesis: Velocity decline and injury tend to arrive together, so a falling trend lowers both the ceiling and the expected remaining exposure; treating them as independent overstates the probability for declining candidates.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether a velocity z-score drop in the last three appearances predicts a 60+ day IL stint within 30 days, controlling for age and workload.

interactions.hypothesis: Park speed offsets bias a candidate's measured ceiling depending on where he pitches; a closer whose home park reads hot appears closer to the threshold, and the contract settles on that biased reading.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare candidates' home and road 99th-percentile speeds after removing league-wide park offsets estimated from visiting pitchers.

interactions.hypothesis: When the best candidate ceilings sit more than about 2 mph under the line the physical exceedance probability is near zero and the anomaly rate sets P(YES); only when a candidate's ceiling approaches the line does the physical tail dominate, so the weight on each route switches with the ceiling gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Across seasons, compare the count of live-feed readings above 105 mph that survive in corrected Savant data against the count of physical pitches above 104.5; check which grows with ceiling gap.

nonlinearities.shape: near-zero then sharply rising, bounded tail in distance to threshold
nonlinearities.why: Exceedance probability is effectively zero for ceilings more than about two mph below the line and rises steeply over the last mph, so a 0.5 mph change in a candidate's peak can change the season probability by an order of magnitude.

nonlinearities.shape: concave saturating: 1 - exp(-N p)
nonlinearities.why: Additional near-peak pitches add diminishing probability once N x p is large; for this threshold N x p is tiny, so the response is nearly linear and exposure late in the season matters proportionally.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at the decimal boundary
nonlinearities.why: Measurement error matters only for readings within a few tenths of 107.0; one-decimal rounding and the 107.0+ versus 107+ wording create a step around the line.

mechanism_review.summary: A velocity-threshold contract settles on the single fastest tracked pitch, so it is an extreme-value problem on a physically bounded quantity. Each pitcher has a speed ceiling set by his arm; only a handful sit within two mph of the threshold, and 107 mph is beyond any tracked pitch to date. Within a pitcher, each fastball's speed equals his current baseline plus situational lifts (leverage, postseason adrenaline, rest, warm air, early in the outing) minus fatigue and paced effort as a starter. The probability of crossing the line is roughly one minus the product, over the remaining near-peak fastballs, of the chance each stays below, so volume of max-effort pitches and health (exposure) multiply the per-pitch tail. Finally the reading itself is a measurement with park calibration error and rounding, which matters at the edge, and with the line above any tracked pitch a gross feed error that is published, and perhaps later corrected, may be a more probable route to YES than the physical tail.

stages.name: Candidate pool and arm ceiling
stages.description: Identify the pitchers whose tracked peaks lie close to the threshold: current MLB relievers and starters with season maxima of 103 mph and higher, plus AAA prospects with tracked peaks that could be called up. Each candidate's ceiling drifts with age, mechanics and health. Because the distribution of pitcher ceilings has a hard upper edge, the any-pitcher probability is carried by two or three arms at most.
stages.distribution: Bounded upper tail (Weibull-domain extreme value with a finite endpoint); pool size is a small discrete count of arms.

stages.name: Health, role and remaining exposure
stages.description: For each candidate, how many near-peak fastballs remain: games left, his role (one-inning closer versus paced starter), the chance of a role change, workload caps, IL status and the forward hazard of an arm injury, and postseason games weighted by his club's probability of playing them. Exposure shrinks over the season and collapses for a candidate who is shut down.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated count of near-peak fastballs; heavy left mass from injury shutdowns; postseason adds a lumpy mixture over rounds.

stages.name: Per-pitch speed given situation
stages.description: Each fastball's speed is the pitcher's baseline for that day plus lifts for leverage, postseason, days of rest, pitch number within the appearance, two-strike counts and temperature. Record-level pitches occur in a narrow set of situations: rested, warm, high-leverage or playoff, first few pitches of an appearance. Small additive lifts change the tail probability by large factors.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal body per pitcher-day with a short, bounded right tail; day-level random effect induces correlation among pitches in one outing.

stages.name: Extreme aggregation over the season
stages.description: Combine per-pitch exceedance probabilities across all remaining near-peak pitches and candidates: P(named) = 1 - product over his pitches of (1 - p), P(any) = 1 - product over candidates. Pitches within a day and pitchers sharing parks or calibration are not independent, and fitting a tail beyond the observed record needs a bounded generalised-Pareto shape rather than an exponential extrapolation.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcome from a max over thousands of correlated draws; probability highly sensitive to the tail shape parameter near the endpoint.

stages.name: Measurement and settlement
stages.description: The deciding reading is a Hawk-Eye release-speed measurement with park-specific offsets, possible post-game revision and one-decimal display; the named series uses 107.0+, the any-pitcher series 107+. The rules include playoffs but do not name a source, so a stadium radar or broadcast figure above 107 that Statcast does not confirm is an unresolved edge. A second route to YES is non-physical: a glitch or mis-tagged speed in the live feed that is published at game time and later corrected, whose settlement treatment is unstated.
stages.distribution: Small symmetric measurement error of a few tenths of a mph, decisive only near the line, plus a rare heavy-tailed gross-error component (feed glitches, mis-tags) that can dominate P(YES) when the physical tail is near zero.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXMLBFASTPITCH settles YES if the named pitcher (sample: Jacob Misiorowski) records a pitch at or above the strike (107.0 MPH) in any game of the stated season, regular season and playoffs included; KXMLBSTAT (sample) settles YES if any pitcher records a 107+ MPH pitch in any game of the season including playoffs. A single pitch suffices. The text does not name the tracking source, does not define how a reading like 106.95 is rounded, and does not say whether spring training, exhibitions or All-Star Game pitches count.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named; presumed MLB Statcast (Hawk-Eye) release speed as published on Baseball Savant / MLB game feed.
variants_and_edge_cases: Named-pitcher (KXMLBFASTPITCH, ladder strikes via floor_strike 107 with greater_or_equal) versus any-pitcher (KXMLBSTAT, custom strike) construction; P(any) >= P(named) for the same threshold.
'107.0+' versus '107+': whether a reading displayed as 107.0 after rounding from 106.95-106.99 counts is not defined.
'any game during the ... season (regular season and playoffs)' leaves spring training and the All-Star Game unaddressed; a position player pitching also counts as 'any pitcher'.
No resolution source is named (Statcast release speed versus stadium radar or broadcast readings can differ), and later data revisions are not addressed.

KXMLBSTAT is a generic season-stat series; this record covers it only for velocity markets such as KXMLBSTAT-26P107-AP, other KXMLBSTAT markets may settle on different stats and are recorded in series_mapping_issues.
A reading published in the live feed or broadcast and later corrected or removed: whether it counts is unstated (velo_first_vs_revised_reading).
